options, none free. (a) Pull the marker inboard of 37.5 m -- a ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h change, but it DECOUPLES the authored marker from the recipe landmark, which is the coupling U12's shape exists to enforce. (b) Move the pad or the landmark in ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp -- that header warns a recipe change re-measures every ground table in the game. (c) Exempt the gym column from the containment clause -- weakening a deliberate assertion. (a) looks cheapest but trades away the invariant that makes these anchors auditable, so it is a ruling rather than a worker's pick.","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/69","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"ZM-69 (Gym 1 door): where should the Thornacre gym-door ground column go, given the recipe's own FromGym landmark fails the pad-containment clause by construction?","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"open","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"high","osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-08-25","x8xpkuruebvskqi2lckjm1o7":"The Thornacre gym door and its FromGym spawn marker each need their own MEASURED ground column -- ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h:613-619 is explicit that a sensor reading its neighbour's column is 'part-buried or hovering with every scale constant still correct', and the two nearest existing columns are ~750 m away on separately-eroded ground. But the natural site fails an existing invariant: ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp:185 puts the 'Gym' pad at centre (760, 864) with m_fFlattenRadius = 50.0, and :214 puts the 'FromGym' landmark at (760, 28, 814) -- EXACTLY 50.0 m from that centre. fTH_PAD_CONTAINMENT_FRACTION = 0.75 (ZM_Tests_ThornacrePlacement.cpp:76) gives a 37.5 m limit, so a column on the recipe's own landmark REDS the same clause U12/U13 apply to the route-gate anchors. Verified independently by the orchestrator against all four constants. The 'Gym' landmark itself is at the pad centre (0 m) and is fine.","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"zenithmon"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T20:23:12.807995","updated_at":"2026-08-25T20:23:12.807995","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor"},{"id":"binn14eenp8ezfsowtod5n7t","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"FIXED in the previous board 05408ef, and the premise was wrong in a way worth recording. docs sync was never hanging and had never failed to complete its WORK: it opened a WebSocket session for EVERY page (199 on this checkout, 597 across the three projects that map to it), including every page already identical to its source, at a handshake plus 2x DEFAULT_SETTLE_MS each and two sessions per replace. A no-op sync therefore ran about ten minutes and every caller's timeout killed it around page 40 of 199, discarding the --json report (emitted at the end) and leaving a zero-byte log. That is exactly why the mirror always looked CURRENT for docs sorting early (Status, DecisionLog) and never for Conventions -- the pages were being written correctly the whole time. syncPage now answers the no-write case from the persisted row with no socket, using the same decideWrite predicate the live path applies, and takes that path ONLY for a clean 'unchanged' (a CONFLICT and --force both still open the session). Measured on this checkout: five consecutive timeouts at 120-300s became exit 0 in 9 SECONDS. Write path re-verified by editing one doc: updated 2, verified true, on exactly the two pages the change touched, 595 skipped. Consequence for the protocol: tick.md step 7's 'timed out -- the mirror is one commit behind is a legal and expected work-log outcome' rests on a false premise and should be retired along with the timeout wrapper it justifies.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"tick.md step 7 mandates `timeout 120 zagent docs sync --json` and documents three prior hangs (300s, 120s, 120s), stating it 'has never once completed'. ZM-67 is the fourth: killed at 120s, zero-byte log, exit 143. The timeout mitigation works and the tick correctly continued -- but a mandated step with a 0/4 success rate is not a step, it is a ritual, and it costs two minutes of every tick that touches a doc. Either fix the WebSocket path it depends on or drop it from the mandated flow and make the mirror an explicit human-run command.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"nuisance","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Fix or retire `zagent docs sync`. It has now hung on FOUR consecutive ticks and has never once completed.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/67","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T09:41:02.14582","updated_at":"2026-08-26T00:37:10.822","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"ddl5rcbext98gjo8rptucf7b","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Shipped: `zagent update` takes --label/--unlabel (flags.ts COMMAND_FLAGS.update), so a marker can be applied AFTER filing, which is when you learn one is needed. The follow-on it asked about also shipped: `windowed` was split into needs-gpu and needs-human (the previous board's migration 0028).","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Labels can only be set at CREATE time. `zagent create` takes --label, but `zagent update` accepts only --priority/--points/--severity/--repro/--environment/--due and answers \"Nothing to update -- pass at least one field\" for --label. So a ticket that is DISCOVERED to need a human after filing cannot be protected. That matters because `windowed` is the board's one mechanical guard for unrunnable work -- filtered from the claim query, contract-invalid on a targeted claim -- and it is exactly the guard you want to apply after reading a ticket, not before. Concrete case: ZM-56 is \"ZM_InteriorTintPixels_Test passes windowed, or is retired with a recorded reason\". It is a requiresGraphics test, so a headless loop cannot run the fix branch and can only verify the RETIRE branch -- an agent handed \"fix it or delete it\", unable to test a fix, deletes coverage. It carries labels tech-debt,visual and is not marked windowed, so nothing stops the loop claiming it. The protection is prose in tick.md, which is precisely the shape of guard this repo keeps finding does not hold.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Add --label / --unlabel to `zagent update`, taking the same comma list `create` already accepts. That alone makes `windowed` applicable on discovery, which is when you actually learn a ticket needs a person. Worth considering a second label for the distinct case ZM-56 represents: not \"needs a windowed run to PRODUCE the deliverable\" (what windowed means today) but \"the only branch a headless agent can complete is the destructive one\". Those want the same queue filtering and different explanations to whoever picks it up.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/49","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-21","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-21T11:40:32.943824","updated_at":"2026-08-23T20:54:24.582","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"f8tg2z23sdabbtt7jkx2ap7t","values":{"dnzedm3e8obk7b1b7bjpti6e":"Leave it stacking. Three reasons: it is consistent with money, which already stacks by ruling; it adds no ZM_GameState state, which ZM-D-135 forbids; and it is MOOT in production because the defeat flag gates re-battles, so the second win cannot occur through normal play. I read DoD item 5 as scoped to the badge -- 'the badge count is right' is the measurable clause and 'double-grant' is the badge verb. If that reading is wrong the fix is one line, gating the Bag::Add on !m_xBag.Has(xRow.m_eItemReward), and it would want its own decision entry because it diverges from the money precedent.","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/70","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"ZM-70: on a REPEAT win over a gym leader the badge is idempotent but the TM item stacks to a second copy. Is that right, or should the item dedupe too?","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"resolved","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"low","osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-08-26","pfp140d5cgrhvbsth95eskme":"ANSWERED, and the guess recorded above was WRONG. The item must deduplicate, and it now does -- ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState gates the grant on ZM_Bag::Has(xRow.m_eItemReward). The independent review found the ZM-D-135 money precedent does not transfer: ZM-D-208's correction (DecisionLog.md:165-172) states money's cause explicitly -- it pays again BECAUSE ZM-D-135 forbids a new ZM_GameState member to record 'already paid' -- and for an item that cause is absent, since m_xBag IS the record and ZM_Bag::Has already answers it, so gating costs no state at all. My 'adds no ZM_GameState state' was therefore an argument FOR gating, which I had recorded as an argument against. The consequence was also not cosmetic as I assumed: Verdant Lash is m_bConsumable = false, so a second copy has exactly one use -- ZM_ShopSell converting it to its 500 sell price -- a FARMABLE PRIZE, the precise shape ZM-D-208's postscript says the per-trainer defeat flag exists to forbid. So DoD item 5 was genuinely UNMET and would have merged Done on my reading. Recorded as ZM-D-214; ZM-D-213 corrected in place. The general lesson, now in tick.md: a ruling's WHY is what decides whether it transfers, and reading only its DECISION is how a non-transferable precedent looks binding.","x8xpkuruebvskqi2lckjm1o7":"DoD item 5 reads 'Awarding twice does not double-grant, and the badge count is right after a repeat win.' The badge is structurally idempotent -- AwardBadge ORs one bit -- so the badge half needs no code and is proven by TrainerReward_SecondWinDoesNotDoubleAwardTheBadge. The ITEM half is the open question: ZM_Bag::Add on a second win yields 2 copies of ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH. The worker let it stack, citing the shipped precedent that prize MONEY is also paid again on a repeat win, because ZM-D-135 makes 'pay once' a CALLER-side gate (the sight FSM / defeat flag) rather than this primitive's job. The unit proves the actual behaviour rather than asserting an assumed one.","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"zenithmon"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-26T09:31:09.713362","updated_at":"2026-08-26T09:59:05.98","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor"},{"id":"fg8c32kskt513f9w1gbr4gxx","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Done, with one deliberate difference in mechanism worth recording.  The outcome this row argued for is in place: a cross-cutting item is now worked only when somebody pulls it into the ACTIVE milestone sprint with zagent sprint add, which is what Roadmap.md already said should happen. The four enforcement proposals it endorsed from the original row have all shipped (see gqbpgj4s).  It was NOT done by flipping the Cross-cutting sprint to non-continuous. Strict IN_SCOPE_SPRINT reaches the same place from the claim query instead: once a project has a non-continuous ACTIVE stage, a continuous bucket stops qualifying, so the sprint row keeps its honest description of itself and the queue stops honouring it while a stage runs. That preserves the reason continuous was added in the first place - a board with no stage in progress still offers the bucket - which flipping the flag would have destroyed.  Your reading of the evidence held up exactly. Re-homing by content would indeed have moved about one ticket, and the other three are correctly stage-less: doctor now reports all four by key rather than proposing false milestone homes for them.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"CORRECTION to the milestone-ordering row filed minutes earlier in this database. Two things in it were overstated and a human triaging it should have the accurate version. (1) I wrote that the 'Cross-cutting - no stage' sprint holds 18 issues 'all claimable regardless of the active milestone'. The sprint holds 18, but only FOUR are actually claimable today: ZM-63, ZM-51, ZM-52, ZM-59. The rest are needs-human, deferred, blocked, or epics. Separately, the seven tickets showing sprint '(none)' are ALL epics, which are never claimable - so hole A's only real victims were ZM-65 and ZM-66, the two tickets the loop itself filed during S8, both since moved into S8 by hand. Hole A is still real and still self-worsening, but its blast radius today is 2, not 7. (2) I did not account for Roadmap.md's explicit design intent. Roadmap.md states of the cross-cutting epics: 'These four epics carry items the stage plan has never had a home for... These have no stage gate. They are scheduled against sprints and releases on the board, not against S0-S12.' So the cross-cutting EPICS (ZM-14 engine gaps, ZM-15 tech debt, ZM-16 open questions, ZM-17 test infra, ZM-18 visual polish) are deliberate and correct, and re-homing their children into S8-S12 by content would contradict the living doc.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"board","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"The defect is narrower and sharper than the first row implied. Roadmap.md says cross-cutting work is 'scheduled against sprints' - and a CONTINUOUS, always-in-scope sprint is precisely the arrangement under which it is never scheduled and always claimable. So the fix is not to re-home 18 tickets; it is to make the 'Cross-cutting - no stage' sprint non-continuous. A cross-cutting item then gets worked only when someone pulls it into the ACTIVE milestone sprint via zagent sprint add, which is exactly what Roadmap.md describes, and it makes 'only tasks in the current sprint are picked up' true without inventing false milestone homes for genuinely stage-less work. On the evidence, re-homing by content would move about ONE ticket (ZM-63, a live quality failure in shipped content that also blocks ZM-56); ZM-51 and ZM-52 are open questions under ZM-16 and ZM-59 is polish debt under ZM-18, all correctly stage-less. The four enforcement proposals in the original row stand unchanged - they are what makes any of this hold.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T00:19:36.817731","updated_at":"2026-08-24T12:55:00.156","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"fpaktmht5fjuo54ldmpx75vb","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"0 of the 15 gate lines in zagent.project.json name a _False config -- every one is --headless, i.e. Null_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True with ToolsEnabled ON. So no gate can compile anything under the #else of #ifdef ZENITH_TOOLS. ZM-67 added exactly that (an ZM_EnsurePropBaked stub plus a newly-unconditional include) and the whole gate list was structurally incapable of building it; a reviewer had to point it out and the orchestrator ran the build by hand. CI DOES have such a step (zm-tests.yml:104-122 builds Zenithmon as D3D12_vs2022_Debug_Win64_False, comment: '_False omits editor/tools'), but branching is direct and push is false, so CI never runs before the commit lands on master -- the break would surface later on a commit several tickets deep. CLAUDE.md already requires gate lines be copied VERBATIM from CI and names zagent.project.json a downstream consumer in the same commit; CI grew this step and the gate list did not. Same shape as the recorded backend-rot lesson, rotated onto the tools axis.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Add a non-tools (_False) build line to each category's gate list, copied verbatim from the CI step that already exists.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/67","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"rejected","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"The premise no longer holds: FOUR gate lines name a _False config, one per game with a CI counterpart -- zagent.project.json:68 (Zenithmon), :149 (Engine/Combat), :192 (DevilsPlayground), :237 (ScriptTest), all D3D12_vs2022_Debug_Win64_False. Each matches its workflow step verbatim: zm-tests.yml:105-121, cb-tests.yml:117, dp-tests.yml:145, st-tests.yml:110. Checked every workflow for a _False build step the gate lists lack and found none. The one _False build that is NOT mirrored is engine-gate.yml:93-124's Sentinel link proof (Vulkan_ and Null_ _False), which is a leaf-purity check on separate projects rather than a per-game tools-off build -- a different question, and filing it here would re-open this row on a claim it never made."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T09:41:01.585999","updated_at":"2026-08-25T09:41:01.585999","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"gmqmgavqr4fl38l8f8rlpm0z","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Option (1) shipped in Zenith bf6d6707, which this row called the real fix. `zagent create` greps the living-doc dirs for the key it just allocated and warns naming every file:line -- client-side and AFTER the create, because the board would need the 932 KB docs tree uploaded to grep it, and the key the board ACTUALLY allocated beats predicting the next one. Option (2), documenting the convention, was deliberately NOT taken as the close: prose in front of a check is the defect this repo keeps naming. The guard was inert when first written (it read $result.key; the key is under payload) and is now a tested function, Get-CreatedKey. The DANGLING direction this does not cover -- a bare key citing a ticket that never existed -- is filed as ZEN-8.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Filing a ticket can silently CAPTURE a phantom forward-reference in the docs, turning a dangling cross-reference into one that resolves to the wrong real ticket. Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Questions.md tagged Q-2026-08-14-001 as [ZM-50 / ZEN-2], meaning \"tracked as ZM-50 on the ZM board and ZEN-2 on the engine board\". ZEN-2 did not exist -- it was aspirational, and ZEN-3..6 still do not exist. Filing an unrelated engine ticket today allocated key ZEN-2 to it, so that reference now resolves to a terrain-performance ticket that has nothing to do with the wall-clock question. That is strictly worse than the dangling state: a reader who follows it lands somewhere plausible and wrong, and nothing flags it. This is the same species as the dangling ZM-D-177 citation that ZM-53 was filed to fix, with the failure mode upgraded from \"leads nowhere\" to \"leads somewhere false\". Tools/doc_lint.ps1 cannot catch it -- its C6 check resolves markdown LINKS, and these are bare bracketed keys in prose.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"board","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Two options, not exclusive. (1) At file time, warn when the key about to be allocated is already cited in any living doc under the categories' docs dirs -- the board knows the next key and the client already uploads the docs tree for sync, so the check costs one grep and would have caught this exactly. (2) Make the convention explicit in AgentBriefing/CLAUDE.md: never write a ticket key into a doc until the ticket EXISTS, because keys are allocated sequentially and a forward reference is a booby trap that arms itself later. Prefer describing the work (\"an engine-side twin, unfiled\") over inventing a key for it.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/49","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-21","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-21T09:22:37.15612","updated_at":"2026-08-23T21:17:39.291","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"gqbpgj4sav9u8bdzn6rncdjp","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"All four enforcement proposals in this row have shipped, board-side, across three commits in the previous board's repo.  (1) The claim query refuses a ticket outside the project ACTIVE sprint. IN_SCOPE_SPRINT is strict now but self-configuring rather than absolute: a project with a non-continuous ACTIVE stage offers that stage ONLY, so both the sprint_id IS NULL and the continuous exemptions stop qualifying, while a board with no stage in progress keeps its previous behaviour unchanged. (17be92f)  (2) zagent create defaults --sprint to the ACTIVE stage, and warns by name when no --parent is set. That closes the hole the loop itself widened every time it filed a follow-up mid-stage. (17be92f)  (3) A stage cannot be completed while its work is unfinished, and the refusal names the tickets that are not done. Since startSprint already refuses a second ACTIVE sprint, completing the current one is the only route to starting the next, which makes this the enforcement point you asked for. --force still carries work to the backlog, because a stage sometimes genuinely ends with scope unlanded; it just has to be deliberate. (17be92f)  (4) zagent doctor grows a queue row per project counting To Do work that is ready and parked outside the ACTIVE stage. It reads 4 on ZM right now: ZM-63, ZM-51, ZM-52 and ZM-59. It counts UNSCHEDULED work apart from work in a later stage, because nothing will ever un-park the first kind, and it goes red only when the queue is ALSO dry, which is the incident it exists to explain. A permanently red check is one nobody reads. (af1873b)","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Milestone ordering is not enforced, so the queue hands out work from outside the ACTIVE sprint. The mapping itself is right: sprints are one-per-milestone (S8 ACTIVE, S9-S12 PLANNED, matching Roadmap.md S0..S12) and the PLANNED gate works - ZM-45, ZM-46 and ZM-37 all correctly report OUT OF STAGE. What leaks is everything that never enters that gate. HOLE A: a ticket with NO sprint is claimable, and create never assigns one - zagent show prints '(none - claimable, sprints are optional)'. This is self-worsening, because the loop files follow-ups during a milestone and every one lands outside milestone control: ZM-65 and ZM-66, both filed by the loop during S8 today, had no sprint until added by hand, and ZM-17 still shows none. HOLE B: the 'Cross-cutting - no stage' sprint is continuous/always-in-scope and holds 18 issues claimable regardless of the active milestone. Its members are not stage-less chores - ZM-51 (player gender), ZM-52 (LFS question), ZM-59 (NPC palette), ZM-63 (PlayerHome tint) are ordinary feature/bug work that belongs to some milestone. Concretely: with ZM-22 finishing Blocked, ZM-23/R1-5 stays blocked, and the next tick would have claimed ZM-63 - Cross-cutting - while S8 is the active milestone. HOLE C: nothing requires the ACTIVE sprint to be complete before the next is started; S8 stands at 21/81 pts over 14 issues.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"board","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"blocks-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Requested behaviour from the repo owner: one sprint per milestone, the current milestone sprint tracked, ONLY tasks in the current sprint picked up, and the next sprint startable only when every task in the current one is complete. Enforcement, all board-side: (1) the claim query refuses any ticket not in the project ACTIVE sprint - which means retiring both 'sprints are optional' and the continuous/always-in-scope exemption, or reducing the latter to something explicit, rare and audited; (2) zagent create requires --sprint, or defaults it to the ACTIVE sprint, so a ticket that cannot be routed to a milestone fails at FILE time exactly as a missing --complexity already does - this is the hole the loop itself widens every time it files a follow-up; (3) zagent sprint start refuses unless every issue in the current ACTIVE sprint sits in a DONE-category status, naming the ones that do not; (4) zagent doctor grows a row counting claimable tickets outside the ACTIVE sprint, which today would read 18+ and is reported nowhere. Precedent for the shape: zagent board status already exits 1 on Roadmap drift, so the drift-detection habit exists - it just does not cover sprint membership.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T00:12:37.669816","updated_at":"2026-08-24T12:55:00.038","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"h9vd7jt0tevtzwmdw5980ibb","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"CRITICAL: zagent claim MUTATES BEFORE IT VALIDATES. A targeted claim on a needs-human ticket (reproduced on ZM-64) writes 'status: To Do -> In Progress' and 'assignee: none -> the agent', THEN returns exit 4 refusing it. The ticket is left assigned, In Progress, and holding the I5 one-ticket-per-repo lock - a following 'zagent next' returned exit 5 (repo busy). So one /tick <needs-human-key> deadlocks the whole queue for every project this checkout serves, and tick.md step 2 ('targeted exit 4: report the error and change nothing') guarantees it stays deadlocked. needs-human's stated contract is 'never claimed, by the queue or by name' - it IS claimed by name and only refused after. FIX: run the needsHuman/EPIC gate before the transaction (zagent check already evaluates both without writing), or roll back to previousStatus + clear assignee on contract failure.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"ZEN-79: does NOT reproduce against Vault; no production change needed. executeOperation (Tools/Vault/server/operations.mjs) calls prepare() at line 321 and writes/commits the journal at 368-369, so no board byte and no commit can exist before a change set is returned; every refusal in claim's prepare (cli/write.mjs:621-656) throws before the changes array is built at 653. Proven by Tools/Vault/test/claim-refusal-atomicity.test.mjs (5 tests: needs-human, EPIC, blocked, queue-empty, plus a non-vacuous accepted-claim control). The eight stale assignments of 2026-09-19 (ZEN-3/12/14/16/18/19/20/22) were imported already-assigned by 3f7b3a59 from the frozen SQL-board snapshot, where this defect WAS real - fossils, not a live Vault defect."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:11.698821","updated_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:11.698821","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"hnwqek3tsl65ybdo54s9nauc","values":{"fgvpu8fja84411t89jvzgvs0":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"open","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"high","kutn19z061622yllp5eqj5ah":"zenithmon","qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"Npc_AuthoredAppearancesAreMutuallyDistinct ratchets on ZM_NPC_COUNT but NOTHING asserts how much headroom is left. The palette space is 36 cells (outfit x hairColour - the blend reads neither skin, build, attachment nor hair style); the 7 authored rows plus the blockout grey have consumed all of it, leaving exactly one free cell that no ZM_HUMAN_ID occupies. The exhaustion happened when Aster took the cast to 7, and nothing went red then - it surfaced three slices later as ZM-23, an IMPOSSIBLE ticket, after a full opus worker dispatch. The general rule: a ratchet on a FINITE RESOURCE that only asserts the current rows are valid cannot report that the next row has nowhere to go, so it always fails at the slice that NEEDS the resource rather than the slice that CONSUMED it.","rlwt4zm5xtrwqk2t2hbwolsx":"Zenithmon / NPC appearance palette + the ratchet that guards it"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T14:45:25.710688","updated_at":"2026-08-24T14:45:25.710688","database_id":"v98et4f3ozbmfonxuavdrrrq"},{"id":"imy6rvk141hta1vnb6bk4622","values":{"dnzedm3e8obk7b1b7bjpti6e":"Option C - append an outfit slot (e.g. ZM_HUMAN_OUTFIT_FORAGER) and/or a hair colour. Both enums are append-only and save-stable, a new slot adds a whole row/column of cells, and it moves NO existing NPC colour by a single float. The alternatives are worse: (A) new ZM_HumanData rows cannot work alone, only one free cell exists; (B) widening the palette basis to read skin/build/attachment moves EVERY existing colour, redding ZM_AutoTests_RivalVesper's material scan and invalidating every value quoted in ZM_HumanData.cpp and Shortfalls.md; (D) re-scoping the invariant to rows that can share a frame needs a scene column on ZM_NpcData that does not exist. This is a CONTENT decision (new authored colours) and the agent loop declined to take it unilaterally.","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"How should the NPC greybox appearance palette gain headroom? It has ZERO free appearances, so no new NPC of any kind can be authored until this is ruled on.","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"resolved","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"high","osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-08-24","pfp140d5cgrhvbsth95eskme":"RULED: option C. Append an outfit slot and/or a hair colour to gain headroom for R1-5. Both enums are APPEND-only and save-stable, a new outfit adds a row of 6 candidate cells and a new hair colour a column of 6, and no existing NPC colour moves by a single float - so no committed scene, material scan or quoted value is disturbed. Rejected: (A) new ZM_HumanData rows cannot work alone, only one cell (TRAVELER+BLONDE) is free and R1-5 needs two; (B) widening the palette basis to read skin/build/attachment moves EVERY existing colour, redding ZM_AutoTests_RivalVesper's material scan and invalidating every value quoted in ZM_HumanData.cpp and Shortfalls.md, and it deepens the proxy's entanglement with appearance rather than fixing it; (D) is CORRECT but needs a scene column on ZM_NpcData that does not exist. Two caveats the implementer must carry. FIRST, appending a slot yields CANDIDATE cells, not usable ones: the new outfit's primary and accent must be chosen so every resulting blend clears the 0.15 floor against all existing rows and against the blockout grey (0.52,0.55,0.60). Report the achieved separations rather than asserting them. SECOND, this is a REFILL, not a fix - 6 cells covers R1-5's two and little else. The structural fix is filed as ZM-68 (option D, scene-aware distinctness, S9) and related to ZM-31. Lowering the 0.15 floor was considered and REJECTED: it is the same shape as widening a sight cone to fit a badly-placed anchor, and this codebase's own rule is to move the anchor.","x8xpkuruebvskqi2lckjm1o7":"ZM_GetHumanPaletteColour is 0.45*outfit.primary + 0.25*outfit.accent + 0.30*hair and reads NEITHER skin tone, build, attachment NOR hair style. The usable space is therefore 6 non-themed outfits x 6 non-DYED hairs = 36 cells. Npc_AuthoredAppearancesAreMutuallyDistinct requires 0.15 separation between every pair of NPC rows naming different ids; Npc_EveryAuthoredRowClearsTheBlockoutFallbackGrey adds 0.15 from (0.52,0.55,0.60). Of the 15 existing ZM_HUMAN_IDs outside the 7-row cast, ZERO clear the floor - the best is TRAINER_ANGLER at 0.1350. Exactly ONE cell in the whole space is free (TRAVELER+BLONDE, rgb 0.4145/0.3450/0.2250, nearest neighbour the Warden at 0.1594) and NO ZM_HUMAN_ID stands in it, so even a new ZM_HumanData row could supply only ONE of the two appearances ZM-23 needs. Recomputed independently by the orchestrator from the source tables and corroborated three ways: the worker's analysis, the orchestrator's own script, and Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Shortfalls.md, which already records TRAINER_RANGER at 0.0873 from the Villager and predates this ticket.","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"zenithmon"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T14:45:24.568558","updated_at":"2026-08-24T21:44:57.221","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor"},{"id":"j36jobz82t92s74tjb2diba6","values":{"fgvpu8fja84411t89jvzgvs0":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"open","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"high","kutn19z061622yllp5eqj5ah":"zenithmon","nptzurv3ah03jchmjogdiltg":"ZM-23 (blocked a second time on this)","qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"The survey was done at FILE granularity and records that \"the FSM latch in ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp\" survives. That is true of the Latch_* units and FALSE of three Gate_* units in the same file, which pin the flagless arm of ZM_MayTrainerEngage against the Rambler's ROSTER row rather than a hand-built one: Gate_FlaglessRowKeysOnTheSessionLatchAndIgnoresTheFlag (fixture :2163, reds at :2177 and :2179), Gate_ShippedRosterStillExercisesBothArms (reds at :2300 and :2310), and Gate_PartylessPlayerIsClosedOnBothArms (flagless fixture :2222 — stays GREEN while its stated purpose and its \"the FLAGLESS rambler\" label silently stop holding). The specific miss is that a BY-ROW helper can still be pinned against a ROSTER row; \"the helper takes a row\" reads as \"hand-built fixture, therefore safe\" when it is not. The same survey made the correct call on ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099 and on phase 8, so the method is sound and only the granularity is wrong.","rlwt4zm5xtrwqk2t2hbwolsx":"ZM-D-208 §2 — the \"what survives Ruling 3\" survey"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T00:33:44.298725","updated_at":"2026-08-25T00:33:44.298725","database_id":"v98et4f3ozbmfonxuavdrrrq"},{"id":"j3dtlaueijp4rmklgl5tzkol","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZM-D-209","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-08-25","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"One STORY carried a whole gym -- a scene, a leader battle, a badge award and a teach-move reward -- behind a four-line Definition of Done, and a survey done before dispatching found three separable seams plus a mislabelling. (1) SHAPE: the R1 slice table already splits PURE data and placement from SCENE AUTHORING, for the reason that authoring writes a tracked asset and pure work does not; Gym 1 has exactly that seam. (2) LABELS: ZM-28 carried human-gate, so even the pure data work would have parked at In Review and needed a person before the next slice could start. Only the scene slice wants a visual sign-off, and only it needs needs-gpu -- Gym1.zscen does NOT exist so creating it is headless-legal, but the Thornacre door is a CHANGE to a committed scene, which the .zscen publish guard refuses headless. That distinction is invisible at the whole-gym granularity. (3) PARALLELISM: the 2026-08-25 link audit found S8 composed as a single linear chain, so its queue depth was 1 and any stall stopped the sprint; G1-3 needs no scene, so making it depend on G1-1 rather than on G1-2 gives the sprint two claimable strands instead of one. (4) SCOPE was overestimated: badge state is already complete and persisted (uZM_BADGE_COUNT, m_uBadgeMask, AwardBadge/HasBadge in ZM_GameState.h:89-176, save module 5), and teach-move already exists as ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE -- so G1-3 is a wiring slice, not a systems one, and the bodies say so to stop a worker rebuilding either. The design was NOT invented: GameDesignDocument.md already specifies Thornacre, Fenna (Grass, L13), the Bloom Badge, Verdant Lash and a hedge-maze layout, and all three bodies inline it per I3.","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/28","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"ZM-28 (Gym 1) is SPLIT into three slices: G1-1 ZM-28 data + placement header (PURE, re-authors nothing), G1-2 ZM-69 authors Gym1.zscen + the Thornacre door (needs-gpu + human-gate), G1-3 ZM-70 badge + teach-move on a leader win (PURE). G1-2 and G1-3 both depend only on G1-1 and run in PARALLEL. ZM-29's blocker moves from ZM-28 to ZM-69 AND ZM-70.","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"zenithmon","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"G1-1 carries a headless solvability unit over the declared maze WITH an anti-vacuity arm (a reachability test over an empty room passes vacuously, so at least one wall must be proven to block a shorter route). G1-2 requires two byte-identical windowed boots and a git status showing only the intended scene paths. G1-3 requires a save/load ROUND TRIP for both the badge and the taught move, read back off a reloaded save rather than off the mutated object, plus a by-ROW seam so its coverage cannot be retired by a content change (ZM-D-208 ruling 2's reasoning, applied here)."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T14:59:34.478728","updated_at":"2026-08-25T14:59:34.478728","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1"},{"id":"j8d273n6mblqolueowqxg8bc","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"ZM-67 moved ZM_PROP_COUNT 25 -> 28 and uZM_PROPGEN_VERSION 1 -> 2, and five claims across AssetManifest.md and TestPlan.md went stale with every gate green -- a human reviewer found them. AssetManifest.md has now been added to C1's file list (it was in NO doc_lint file list at all, so it had zero coverage), but that does not close the class, and it is worth being explicit about why rather than assuming it did. C1's regexes match `N tests passing|registered|in the suite|in batch` and `N/M tests`, and its CEILING is the ZENITH_AUTOMATED_TEST_REGISTER count. The stale claims are `Family total: 25 props x 4 = 100 files`, `uZM_PROPGEN_VERSION (currently 1)` and `It ships **8** pure/all-config ZM_Gen units` -- roster arithmetic and version stamps, not test counts, and comparing a unit-count claim against the AUTOMATED registry ceiling would be comparing two different populations. The right shape is a separate check that reads ZM_PROP_COUNT and uZM_PROPGEN_VERSION out of the headers and asserts the doc's stated numbers match, the way C7 already does for the LIVE PIN block against unit_baselines.json.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"nuisance","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"doc_lint needs a check that reconciles AssetManifest.md's roster arithmetic and generator version stamps against the headers. C1 cannot be widened to cover them.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/67","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed, and widened well past the original ask. doc_lint gained C10, modelled on C7 as the row suggested: ground truth read from the headers, exact-equality in either direction, path:line on a violation. It covers ZM_PROP_COUNT roster arithmetic (counting enumerators, not a literal) AND every generator version stamp -- generators are DISCOVERED by globbing Games/<Game>/Source/Gen/ZM_*Gen.h rather than hardcoded, so a sixth generator is covered the day it lands. That widening was worth doing: the original two stale claims were the tip. Measured across both docs, FIVE more were stale -- CREATUREGEN claimed 3 in three places against a header at 6, HUMANGEN claimed 1 in TestPlan against 9, BUILDINGGEN claimed 1 against 5 -- all with every gate green. All corrected: TestPlan keeps its quote-the-number convention, AssetManifest is de-numbered to point at the headers per the policy that file already states about itself at :403-409. A guard on a self-documenting prefix was caught by the new assert script before shipping: ZM_PROP_COUNTER is a real roster row and a textual prefix of the ZM_PROP_COUNT terminator, so the first regex stopped early and counted 17 instead of 32."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T12:54:26.926743","updated_at":"2026-08-25T12:54:26.926743","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"ja6kvxep3eb8fvtfzh66157h","values":{"dnzedm3e8obk7b1b7bjpti6e":"Keep the ordering but make R1-10 re-derive. Either add a Definition-of-Done line to ZM-26 requiring the camera-clearance budget be re-confirmed after the Warden lands, or explicitly record that NPC bodies are out of scope for the clearance budget -- in which case the ZM-24 -> ZM-25 reason should be narrowed to the sample-set/parameterisation work rather than the physics world. Flipping the link is the third option but fights ZM-26's own do LAST instruction.","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/26","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"Should ZM-25 -> ZM-26 be FLIPPED? R1-9 derives a camera-clearance budget that R1-10 then invalidates.","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"open","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"low","osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-08-25","x8xpkuruebvskqi2lckjm1o7":"Found during the 2026-08-25 blocking-link audit. The R1 slice table in Status.md declares R1-10 deps R1-9, and ZM-26's own title says do LAST and in isolation because it re-authors both Dawnmere and Route1 -- so the link is a legitimate risk-isolation ordering and I kept it. But it sits in tension with the reason recorded on the neighbouring edge. ZM-24 -> ZM-25 holds because R1-9 re-derives its budget by raycasting Route 1 columns against the Route 1 PHYSICS WORLD, which R1-6 changes by adding two trainer bodies. R1-10 adds ANOTHER body to that same world (the relocated Warden). By the identical argument, running R1-9 before R1-10 derives a budget against a Route 1 that R1-10 then changes -- the exact staleness the R1-6 dependency exists to prevent, just one slice later. Mitigating: the clearance maths is a function of ground and geometry, and the sample table deliberately carries no rings around NPCs (ZM_AutoTests_CameraClearance.cpp header), so an NPC body may matter less than terrain would.","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"zenithmon"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T11:48:41.731631","updated_at":"2026-08-25T11:48:41.731631","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor"},{"id":"jkuwdlkuht1dr563aey6j8r1","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Shipped: all ten tickets (ZM-20,21,22,23,24,25,26,27,28,31) now read \"Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run\" and none names a pin site -- verified by reading each body, not by sampling. The enabling capability it said was missing, `zagent update --dod`, exists.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"TEN open tickets carry a Definition-of-Done line that is now WRONG and points a worker at protected paths: ZM-20, ZM-21, ZM-22, ZM-23, ZM-24, ZM-25, ZM-26, ZM-27, ZM-28, ZM-31 all say some form of \"Baseline bumped in Status.md AND zm-tests.yml AND zagent.project.json\". Since b6f211d6 the pin has ONE home, Tools/unit_baselines.json, and the workflows and zagent.project.json name the GAME instead of a number. Two of the three sites those DoDs name are protectedPaths, so a worker that follows the inlined DoD literally edits files zagent guard refuses and the ticket Blocks on work that is now a one-line edit to an unprotected file. The DoD is inlined verbatim into the worker prompt by I3, so it competes directly with tick.md step 6, which now carries the correct instruction. Giving a worker two conflicting instructions and hoping it picks the right one is not a contract.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"contract","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Rewrite that DoD line once across the ten tickets to \"Every affected game's row bumped in Tools/unit_baselines.json from an OBSERVED run\". The CLI cannot edit DoD text (update takes --points/--severity/--priority, not the body), and commenting requires claiming each ticket because of the ownership guard, so ten claims to fix ten sentences is worse than the problem -- this wants a board-side edit or a bulk update command. Longer term the DoD should not name pin SITES at all: it is duplicating a fact that changes, which is the same duplication the manifest refactor removed from the build. \"Bump the pinned baseline from an observed run\" says everything a worker needs and cannot go stale when the plumbing moves.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/49","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-21","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-21T11:39:14.542917","updated_at":"2026-08-23T20:54:24.68","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"jnwzpe1xzrt1h15vhs4bc7qa","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"I3's inline list omits RECORDED RULINGS, and that is what broke ZM-23. I3 says paste the ticket body, the DoD, the file list and the conventions. On ZM-23 all four were pasted and the worker still shipped a trainer row violating DecisionLog ZM-D-203 Ruling 3 ('both get their own ZM_STORY_FLAG_ID', because a flagless trainer's prize is farmable across restarts) - and pinned the violation with a NEW test asserting it was correct. Nothing could catch it: contractValid checks routing, the reachability scan checks paths, the drift resolver checks that citations RESOLVE, and three pre-existing units actively require a flagless row so the violation was the only state that passed. It surfaced only because risk MEDIUM happens to sit in reviewOn. FIX: (1) add rulings to I3's list; (2) mechanise it - zagent.project.json already declares decisionLog and decisionIdPrefix, so the claim could resolve candidate rulings into .zagent/run/<KEY>/rulings.md the way it already writes drift.txt; (3) add 'the ticket's subject matter is governed by a recorded decision' to the review.required OR.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Item (1) landed: invariant I3 at tick.md:66-70 now reads 'Paste the ticket body, the Definition of Done, the file list, the conventions AND EVERY RECORDED RULING that governs the ticket's subject matter into the worker prompt', with the ZM-23 / ZM-D-203 incident written up directly below at tick.md:72-93 naming decisionLog and decisionIdPrefix. Items (2) mechanise it as .zagent/run/<KEY>/rulings.md and (3) the third review.required OR term are NOT done and are tracked on the still-open 2026-08-24 audit wrap-up row, which carries them as halves (4) and (3) -- resolving them here would lose the only remaining record of the mechanisation half."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:12.748937","updated_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:12.748937","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"jrrg1kgsy349kvzs30xf5ogn","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed exactly as requested (39b24437 + ae475483): 'zagent finish --status Done' now refuses a work log carrying an unticked Definition-of-Done box and names each one, enforced client-side before the request leaves. Blocked and In Review are deliberately unaffected. tick.md step 7 gains the missing third arm (green-but-DoD-unmet is Blocked). Verified live both ways against real ZM-23 and ZM-65 work logs. +4 assertions.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"tick.md step 7 branches on GATE COLOUR ONLY, so a green partial reaches Done with the DoD unmet. The only branches are Green -> commit + finish Done, and Red -> fix forward -> Blocked. There is no branch for a worker returning a correct partial with a verified impossibility, which is what ZM-23 did: gates green on what landed, two of three DoD boxes unticked. An unattended loop reads 'Green' and records Done; finish accepts it; the step-8 template renders DoD checkboxes that nothing consults. This is a fail-open path to Done and it is the same defect the protocol names one level down at step 6.5 ('green gates answer a narrower question than they look like they answer'). FIX: have 'zagent finish --status Done' REFUSE when the worklog it is handed carries an unticked DoD box, and name the box - a rule enforced at a check that already fails.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:13.262644","updated_at":"2026-08-24T17:20:11.067","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"l5zosw2taihffor8hps9nkwk","values":{"fgvpu8fja84411t89jvzgvs0":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"open","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"medium","kutn19z061622yllp5eqj5ah":"zenithmon","qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"Appending any ZM_STORY_FLAG_ID necessarily edits Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_StoryFlags.cpp, which holds TWO deliberately-literal pins: Registry_ShippedIndicesAreFrozenAndRivalOneIsSix asserts ZM_STORY_FLAG_COUNT == 7u (:343) and ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE == 7u (:346), and Codec_EnumValueIsTheWireBitIndex requires the hand-spelled 7-row axEXPECTED_WIRE_BITS table (:78-89) to name EVERY registered flag. Both are correct and intentional - the point is that an append cannot pass silently. The gap is that this is nowhere documented as a pin site: Docs/SaveFormat.md:263-268 states the append-only rule without naming the file that ENFORCES it, and ZM_StoryFlags.h's own header comment tells you to add a flag here rather than leaving a numeric gap, without saying what else must move. The practical consequence is that a ticket scoped to add a story flag will be filed with a file list that omits the one file the change cannot avoid, which is exactly what happened on ZM-23's fix-forward attempt: the worker prompt instructed 'check whether any unit pins ZM_STORY_FLAG_COUNT and update it if so' while the exhaustive file list omitted the only file that pins it, so the two instructions could not both be obeyed and the worker correctly stopped without editing anything.","rlwt4zm5xtrwqk2t2hbwolsx":"Zenithmon / the story-flag registry has a SECOND pinned site that nothing documents"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T14:45:26.292776","updated_at":"2026-08-24T14:45:26.292776","database_id":"v98et4f3ozbmfonxuavdrrrq"},{"id":"ma0olv4j1tr5lj89h3vhjspv","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"With a ticket in flight, `zagent check` returned exit 5 for an epic (ZM-17), a needs-human ticket (ZM-30) and an out-of-stage ticket (ZM-45) alike. tick.md step 2 states an EPIC comes back exit 4 from check 'on the queue AND by name' -- true only when the repo is idle. check is the one verb documented as writes-nothing/claims-nothing, i.e. the planning tool meant to be safe while something is in flight, which is exactly when it is least informative. And tick.md's standing rule is 'Exit codes are the interface -- branch on them, not on stdout prose', so a caller obeying it cannot distinguish 'this is an epic and never claimable' from 'busy, try later'. The CONTRACT line is still printed, so only the machine-readable half is lost.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"For `zagent check` specifically, let the DURABLE contract verdict (exit 4) win over the TRANSIENT I5 repo-busy verdict (exit 5). Keep 5 winning for claim/next, where the lock is the whole point.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Implemented exactly as scoped. Tools/Vault/cli/read.js:311-320 computes check's exit as: breaker open -> 6; targeted would-claim -> 0; durable blocked (EPIC / needs-human / contract) -> 4; only THEN in-flight -> 5; else 4. So the durable verdict wins for check and the transient lock verdict no longer masks it. The comment at read.js:302-309 records the original symptom (check on an EPIC returned 5 while a ticket was in flight) and states that claim/next are untouched and still return 5 first, which is the half the row asked to preserve."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T00:34:10.293735","updated_at":"2026-08-25T00:34:10.293735","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"mqki0sgp6thvln8sic4yi1yh","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Shipped as option (a), the one this row called preferable: dispatch.ts gateSelection() calls effectiveGates({changedPaths}), so a diff touching Zenith/** unions in the Engine category gates regardless of filing category. No human has to remember to file a twin.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"A ticket's gate list is selected by its filing CATEGORY, never by which directories the diff actually touches. ZM-50 is category Zenithmon but edits Zenith/EntityComponent/Components/Zenith_GraphComponent.Tests.inl -- engine-shared code compiled into the Zenith lib that every game links. So the run executed Zenithmon's four gates and never built or tested Combat, and never checked the engine pin (1638). The ticket's own goal text even says \"the fix is engine-side - this ticket is filed against the ENGINE board on purpose\", so the body and the category disagree and only the category has any mechanical effect. The worker and the independent reviewer both flagged this without being told the other had. Questions.md tags the entry [ZM-50 / ZEN-2], implying an Engine-side twin, but nothing requires ZEN-2 to run, or to run AFTER this commit rather than before it. This is the same shape as the defect ZM-50 itself is about: a shared engine unit rotting invisibly for one game while looking fine for another.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Either (a) derive the gate list from the diff: any change touching Zenith/** unions in the Engine category's gates regardless of filing category, which generalises to any shared top-level directory; or (b) require a hard BLOCKS/BLOCKED-BY link between a category ticket and its cross-category twin, so the claim query's existing mechanical blocker check forces the engine-side verification to happen in the right order. (a) is preferable because it needs no human to remember to file the twin. As a stopgap the orchestrator can run the extra category's gates by hand, which is what this run did -- but that is a convention, not a mechanism, and it is exactly the kind of thing that works until the one time nobody does it.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/50","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-21","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-21T01:23:27.139935","updated_at":"2026-08-23T20:54:24.922","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"mw0i6mvnaxeqbw2vp2k6dshp","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Claiming ZM-28 on 2026-08-25 freshly wrote ticket.json, body.md and drift.txt and left in place, from an earlier attempt on the same key: a tick_gates.json reading state=complete, exitCode=0, verdict='all gates green' at a headSha of a DIFFERENT commit, plus a gates.json whose recorded changed-set was ['Tools/tick_gates.ps1'] -- an unrelated diff -- plus gates.log, gates.prev.log and three gate_*.ps1 scratch scripts. The only thing between that and a tick that skips its gates is a PROSE rule ('if headSha does not match current HEAD, treat it as absent'), which is exactly the shape this repo keeps naming as the defect: a rule in prose standing in front of a check. Get-RecordedGateSelection (ZagentClient.psm1:727) returns the raw file with no headSha, no timestamp and no comparison. The gates.json half is largely self-defending, because the board re-derives the gate LIST from the CURRENT changed set and a mismatch fails -- so it is only invisible when the list is identical, in which case running those gates was right anyway. The tick_gates.json half is defended by nothing mechanical. FIX: make the CLAIM the boundary of an attempt. Archiving to <KEY>.prev/ keeps I6 forensics while making a stale artifact impossible, and it is cheaper and stronger than adding a `zagent verdict` subcommand that the protocol would then have to remember to call.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"zagent claim should archive an existing .zagent/run/<KEY>/ to <KEY>.prev/ so a stale GREEN gate verdict cannot be sitting there when a tick starts.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-26","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Implemented, though not in the PowerShell the row proposed. Tools/Vault/cli/client.mjs:287-294 archivePreviousRun does fs.rm(<KEY>.prev, recursive) then fs.rename(<KEY>, <KEY>.prev), called from writeCompatibilityScratch (client.mjs:317-318) whenever (command==='claim'||command==='next') && result.exitCode===0, BEFORE any new run scratch is written. tick_gates.json lives at .zagent/run/<KEY>/tick_gates.json (Tools/tick_gates.ps1:85) so it is swept into <KEY>.prev on every fresh claim and cannot survive into the new attempt. Get-RecordedGateSelection no longer exists -- ZagentClient.psm1 was gutted to 5 pure helpers when that backend was removed, and the boundary now lives in Node."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-26T00:37:58.169139","updated_at":"2026-08-26T00:37:58.169139","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"nco9z434yy56qmcgt3h7ct8l","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-08-26","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"★ THE DURABLE FINDING, and it is why this is a decision rather than a work-log line: APPENDING A TRAILING ENUM COLUMN TO AN AGGREGATE-INITIALIZED ROW TABLE IS NOT SAFE WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT DEFAULT. `ZM_TrainerData` rows are POSITIONAL aggregate initializers -- the struct's own comment already warns that inserting a column mid-struct shifts every trailing value -- but the danger at the END is different and undocumented. `ZM_BADGE_BLOOM` is enumerator 0, so a trailing `ZM_BADGE_ID` with no default member initializer VALUE-INITIALIZES to 0, i.e. to 'this trainer awards the Bloom Badge'. `Tests/ZM_Tests_TrainerData.cpp` builds SIX hand-built fixtures using only the first nine positional fields, and every one of them would silently have claimed Gym 1's badge. The columns therefore ship with `= ZM_BADGE_NONE` and `= ZM_ITEM_NONE`, which are load-bearing rather than stylistic. SEVEN MORE GYM LEADERS will add reward rows, and the same trap arms itself for every future trailing column whose enum has a meaningful zero. Two further notes for whoever adds the next one. (1) The file that would have caught it was OUTSIDE the worker's permitted write list, and it was found only because a file list bounds WRITES and not READS -- the survey must read wider than it edits. (2) A repeat win does NOT deduplicate the item: `ZM_Bag::Add` yields a second copy, deliberately, because prize MONEY already stacks on a repeat win under ZM-D-135's ruling that 'pay once' is a CALLER-side gate rather than this primitive's job, and gating the item here would diverge from that precedent while adding no state. It is moot in production because the defeat flag gates re-battles. The behaviour is PROVEN by a unit rather than assumed, and an open Questions row on ZM-70 records the reading in case it should be overruled -- the fix would be one line.","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/70","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"ZM-70 (G1-3) wires the leader-win reward onto the SHIPPED write-back seam rather than building anything new. `ZM_TrainerData` gains two trailing columns, `m_eBadgeReward` and `m_eItemReward`; Fenna's row is the first to carry real values (`ZM_BADGE_BLOOM`, `ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH`) and every other row names the NONE sentinels. Per ZM-D-208 Ruling 2's reasoning, which ZM-70 cites, a by-ROW primitive `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool)` is extracted and the by-ID overload becomes classify + is-registered + resolve + forward, so the reward mechanism can be driven by a hand-built fixture row and its coverage cannot be retired by a content change. The badge goes through the existing `ZM_GameState::AwardBadge` mask (save module 5) and the TM through the existing `ZM_Bag::Add` (module 6): NO new ZM_GameState state and NO save-schema change. `Components/ZM_BattleDirector.cpp` needed no edit -- the call site's signature is unchanged. 'Grants Verdant Lash' is implemented as granting the TM ITEM into the bag, not as writing a move into a party monster's `m_axMoves`: there is no item-USE path anywhere in this game, which ZM-D-196 Ruling 1 already established ('no way to USE an item at all'), so the enum value and the data rows exist with ZERO runtime consumers. The heartbeat alternative was not taken.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes is 30, and step 5 says to TaskStop the worker past it and treat the ticket as a failed attempt. Observed worker wall-clock this session: ZM-53 109s, ZM-57 793s, ZM-50 517s then 838s, ZM-49 904s then 499s, ZEN-2 2601s then 935s. ZEN-2's first worker ran 43 minutes -- 45 percent over the guardrail -- and produced the chunk-span design that shipped. Killing it at 30 minutes would have destroyed correct work and cost a full re-dispatch, so the orchestrator let it run and the guardrail silently did not apply. A limit that is right to ignore is worse than no limit: it trains the operator to skip the check, and then it is not there on the run that genuinely wedges. Note the routing tiers make this predictable rather than random -- every run over 15 minutes was opus on a COMPLEX ticket, and every sonnet/haiku run finished well inside 30.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"tick","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Scale the timeout by complexity rather than pinning one number for every ticket: TRIVIAL/SIMPLE keep something tight (10-15 min), MODERATE 30, COMPLEX 60+. The board already knows the complexity -- it is what picks the model -- so this needs no new field. Alternatively make the guardrail a HEARTBEAT rather than a wall-clock cap: kill a worker that has produced no tool call for N minutes, which is what \"wedged\" actually means, instead of one that is simply doing a large job slowly. The gate asserts `ran == Baseline` EXACTLY, so adding one test reds it with zero failures. Bumping the pin means editing every site that carries it, and for Zenithmon two of the three are PROTECTED: Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md (editable), .github/workflows/zm-tests.yml (protected by .github/**), and zagent.project.json (protected). zagent guard refuses both, so step 6.4 Blocks the ticket however green everything else is. A backend-neutral ENGINE unit is worse -- it moves every game's pin plus Tools/run_unit_gate.ps1's default. tick.md said \"the fix is to bump every pinned site in the same commit\" and named both protected files, so the protocol told the loop to do the exact thing its own guard would Block it for. That has been corrected to say park-and-file, and to warn against the tempting wrong fix (deleting the worker's tests to buy a green gate, which looks identical to success on the board). But the underlying limit stands, and it is severe: this repo mandates tests with all new code, so most real feature work is permanently out of the loop's reach. Every ticket run so far has been unit-count-neutral by luck of selection, not by design.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Give the baseline ONE home that is not protected -- e.g. Tools/unit_baselines.json (or a per-game file next to the game), read by run_unit_gate.ps1, referenced by zm-tests.yml, and named rather than duplicated by zagent.project.json's gate line. Then a count change is a one-file edit the loop can make and the guard permits, while .github/** and zagent.project.json stay protected. That also removes the standing four-site sync hazard the docs already warn about repeatedly -- a stale pin reds a REQUIRED check with zero failing tests, which is the same failure this ticket describes, just triggered by a human forgetting a site instead of by the guard. If a single home is not acceptable, the alternative is to accept the limit explicitly: label such tickets so the claim query filters them out the way it already filters `windowed`, so the loop never claims work it provably cannot finish.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/50","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-21","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-21T02:32:31.459231","updated_at":"2026-08-23T20:54:24.861","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"o6wn36un5yk816ple5m6odcf","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"ZM-67's DoD ends 'Before/after captures of all three props recorded in the work log, so the visual sign-off has something to judge', and it is human-gate, so that evidence IS the deliverable. No camera-on-the-props harness existed. A BEFORE image can therefore only come from a tree that has the harness and NOT the change -- which one worker dispatch cannot produce, since a single worker authors both at once. Step 5 reads as one-dispatch-per-ticket and never warns that evidence-producing DoD items constrain authoring ORDER; a loop following it literally lands both together, captures only an AFTER, and silently destroys what the human gate exists for. This is the same shape step 6.2 already documents for PINS in the ZM-65 nine-step order (the freeze goes BETWEEN the two identical boots) -- the lesson was learned for measurements and never generalised to evidence. ZM-67 was run as stage 1 (harness only, appearance frozen) then stage 2 (the visual work).","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"tick","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"blocks-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"tick.md step 5 should say: a Definition of Done that asks for BEFORE evidence ORDERS your dispatches -- the harness that produces the evidence must land, and be run, before the change it measures.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/67","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Landed in .claude/commands/tick.md:1054-1073 as a starred step-5 rule: a DoD that asks for BEFORE evidence ORDERS your dispatches, decide the stages before the first one -- the harness that produces the evidence must land, and be run, before the change it measures. ZM-D-196 Ruling 2 reads 'Explicitly NO gym door'. Read as a decision it forbids ZM-69 outright. Read with its WHY -- 'Gym1 ... declared but unauthored, so a door to an unauthored scene is a permanent black screen' -- it is a PRECONDITION that ZM-69 discharges by authoring Gym1. tick.md already separates a ruling's JUDGEMENT from its SURVEY; this is a third kind, a judgement whose validity is CONDITIONAL on a stated fact, and pasting only the Decision line (which is what 'paste the ruling verbatim' naturally produces) makes a legitimate ticket look like a violation. (2) GREP THE SUBJECT. ZM-69's tripwire table found 4 of 8 sites. The gap has a clean cause: I enumerated files that MENTION 'gym door', and ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry.cpp never uses that phrase -- it says 'the Gym'. The sites that matter ASSERT THE ABSENCE and name the SYMBOL (ZM_SCENE_GYM1, ZM_IsSceneRegisteredForLoad). Step 5's file-list rule currently says 'start from the DoD's nouns and follow them into the repo'; nouns are prose. For a ticket that reverses a recorded assertion the survey pattern must be the identifier. (3) DURABLE FINDINGS NEED A HOME. ZM-28's worker found that appending a move is never inert -- ZM_Learnsets.cpp:52 and ZM_SpeciesData.cpp:555 both DERIVE from the whole move table by scanning it, which no blast-radius grep can find. Seven more gym reward moves remain, so it recurs seven times. I3 tells every tick to GREP the DecisionLog for governing rulings, but no step ever CREATES one from a discovery; step 8's 'Deviations / follow-ups' is a work-log row on a closing ticket that the next worker never reads. One sentence in step 8 fixes it, and the mechanism (zagent decide) already exists. (4) RETIRE THE DOCS-SYNC PROSE. Step 7's 'timed out -- the mirror is one commit behind is a legal and expected work-log outcome', the mandatory `timeout 120` wrapper and the Bash(timeout *) allowed-tools entry all rest on the belief that docs sync hangs and has never completed. It does not: the previous board's 05408ef root-caused it to a WebSocket per page for all 597 pages including unchanged ones, and it now exits 0 in 9 seconds. The machinery and the paragraph should go.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"tick","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Four changes to tick.md, all earned by the 2026-08-25 ZM run: paste a ruling's WHY not just its Decision; grep the SUBJECT not the prose on a reversal ticket; a durable worker finding becomes a DecisionLog entry rather than a work-log line; and retire the docs-sync timeout prose, which now rests on a disproved premise.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-26","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"All four landed in .claude/commands/tick.md: (a) paste the WHY beside the Decision, tick.md:1007 with the ZM-D-196 worked example; (b) on a ticket reversing a recorded assertion the survey pattern is the SYMBOL, tick.md:828 with the ZM_SCENE_GYM1 example; (c) a finding that outlives the ticket is a DecisionLog entry not a work-log line, tick.md:1804 (and zagent finish now refuses a terminal status whose work log carries no Durable findings answer); (d) the mandatory timeout-120 wrapper around docs sync is gone (tick.md:1726 calls it bare) and the prose is reframed as fixed history at tick.md:1729-1738. The false sentence -- 'Running a windowed TEST is not authoring either' -- is deleted and replaced with the measured truth plus the trap it creates on a measure-then-freeze ticket, including that the two-boot proof cannot catch it (two pre-freeze boots are byte-identical to each other, i.e. reproducibly wrong). The nine-step needs-gpu runbook is added, since steps 2 and 5 are the same command with the same success signature. The tick_gates.ps1 dirty-asset assertion was NOT taken -- see the separate note on why conditional gate logic in that script is a bad trade.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"tick.md contradicts itself on windowed tests and the wrong half is load-bearing. Step 2 says 'Running a windowed TEST is not authoring either' while the same section says 'the authoring runs at boot, before the test does'. The second is correct: on ZM-65, running an --automated-test on a Vulkan_*_True build re-authored the committed Dawnmere.zscen as a plain side effect of booting. On a measure-then-freeze ticket this writes the SENTINEL value into a tracked asset (an entity a million metres down, byte count unchanged), because the measuring run necessarily happens while the row is still unfrozen. The two-boot byte-identity proof does NOT catch it - two pre-freeze boots are identical to each other, i.e. reproducibly wrong. FIX: delete the false sentence; state that a windowed _True boot authors before it tests; have tick_gates.ps1 assert no TRACKED asset outside the recorded changed set went dirty.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:12.244118","updated_at":"2026-08-24T17:20:11.586","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"p992isyvwp5t9vag7g4despv","values":{"h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"fixed","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"high","kutn19z061622yllp5eqj5ah":"uncategorized","qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"OPEN DEFECT: replacing the body of a page that ALREADY has content does not land. The client emits a correct ~370-byte append update, the realtime server receives all 376 bytes on the wire, and Yjs integrates it into a ~19-byte no-op with no pending structs - the new blocks simply never appear. Writing to an EMPTY page works every time (74/74 pages created and verified). Reproduced with and without a second client connected, with and without the server touching root types through the second Yjs module copy, and against both a single delete-then-insert and an append-then-delete. NOT root-caused. Mitigated, not fixed: the write is two-phase (append, verify the appended state persisted, only then drop the superseded blocks), so a failed update leaves the page on its PREVIOUS revision and reports verified:false, instead of leaving it blank. Consequence today: the initial mirror is correct and idempotent, but a doc that changes in the repo will report `updated ... verified:false` and the page will keep the old text until this is fixed. Suspect the dual Yjs module instance the server prints on every boot ('Yjs was already imported'). — RESOLVED 2026-08-16. Root cause: TWO copies of Yjs in the realtime server process. y-websocket/bin/utils is CJS and require()s yjs/dist/yjs.cjs; every module we wrote imported yjs/dist/yjs.mjs. bindState seeded a y-websocket doc with the ESM copy, so the store held ESM Items — and an appended item does not carry its parent on the wire, so Yjs recovers it from its left neighbour via `this.left.constructor === Item` (Item.getMissing). Across two copies that identity check is false, parent stayed null, and Item.integrate fell through to `new GC(...)`: the insert was integrated as GARBAGE, silently. Empty pages were unaffected because the first item in a fragment carries its parent name inline; deletes were unaffected because a delete set is applied by id — which is why the naive single-transaction delete+insert blanked pages instead. It only ever reproduced UNBUNDLED (tsx, i.e. dev and the Playwright fleet); esbuild collapsed both importers onto one copy, so the deployed container never had it. Fix: server code takes Yjs from packages/realtime/src/server/yjs.ts (which require()s it, the way y-websocket does), ws-server.ts refuses to boot on a mismatch, and eslint bans the bare import under src/server/. Covered by apps/notion/e2e/docs-sync.spec.ts (\"a page that already has a body is replaced, not left on its old revision\") and packages/realtime/src/server/yjs.test.ts. The two-phase write is KEPT — it is what stopped this from blanking pages.","rlwt4zm5xtrwqk2t2hbwolsx":"zagent docs sync / realtime"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-16T15:05:38.713184","updated_at":"2026-08-16T15:52:33.93434","database_id":"v98et4f3ozbmfonxuavdrrrq"},{"id":"pjl6uhb4b01k1cjqs9npbgcj","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-08-26","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"★ A PRECEDENT WAS APPLIED WITHOUT ITS CAUSE, AND THAT IS THE GENERAL LESSON. The first draft let the item stack, reasoning that prize MONEY stacks on a repeat win under ZM-D-135. But ZM-D-135's correction (ZM-D-208, DecisionLog.md:165-172) states money's cause explicitly: it pays again BECAUSE 'ZM-D-135 forbids a new ZM_GameState member to record it'. For an item that cause is ABSENT -- `m_xBag` IS the record and `ZM_Bag::Has` already answers 'do I own this', so gating adds no state whatsoever. Reading the ruling's DECISION ('money pays again') and not its WHY is what made a non-transferable precedent look binding, which is the same failure mode ZM-D-212 records one entry earlier about surveys, and the same shape the tick protocol now names as a ruling's third kind of sentence. AND THE CONSEQUENCE WAS NOT COSMETIC: Verdant Lash is `m_bConsumable = false` (ZM_ItemData.cpp:129, pinned by ZM_Tests_Gym1Placement.cpp:1206 -- 'TMs in this game are reusable'), so a second copy has exactly ONE use: `ZM_ShopSell` (ZM_ShopLogic.cpp:68-76) converting it to its `m_uSellPrice` of 500. That is a farmable prize -- precisely the shape ZM-D-208's postscript says the per-trainer defeat flag exists to forbid -- so the money precedent would have re-opened the hole the flag was added to close. It is moot in normal play because the defeat flag gates re-battles, which is exactly why no gate would ever have caught it: the assertion was a compiled constant that PASSED, `run_unit_gate` only checks `ran == baseline`, and `doc_lint` does not read C++. ★ SECOND FINDING, and it is why this entry exists rather than a silent edit: the 'load-bearing' default member initializers ZM-D-213 recorded as a DURABLE FINDING shipped with ZERO COVERAGE. Deleting `= ZM_BADGE_NONE` / `= ZM_ITEM_NONE` left every gate green, because all four real rows spell every column and the six fixtures never READ the new ones -- a comment asserting a guard exists, which ZM-D-212 already names as worse than no guard. Closed with a compile-time nine-field aggregate probe plus two static_asserts in `ZM_TrainerData.h`, needing no test file and moving no unit count. Note the trap is wider than first recorded: item enumerator 0 is `ZM_ITEM_CATCHORB`, a REAL item, not only `ZM_BADGE_BLOOM`.","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/70","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"ZM-D-213's item-reward reasoning is CORRECTED before the commit: a repeat win over a gym leader now DEDUPLICATES the take-home item. `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState` gates the grant on `ZM_Bag::Has(xRow.m_eItemReward)`, so `m_bItemGranted` is false and the bag count stays 1 on a second win. The badge was already idempotent by its own structure (AwardBadge ORs one bit) and prize MONEY still stacks. Three columns, three mechanisms, and the header now states three reasons instead of arguing both sides. ZM-D-213's board row predates the review and still carries the superseded reasoning; the repo-local entry has been corrected in place and points here.","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"zenithmon","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"`TrainerReward_SecondWinDoesNotDoubleAwardTheBadge` now asserts the badge count stays 1 AND the TM count stays 1 with `m_bItemGranted` false on the second win -- it previously asserted the count reached 2. `TrainerReward_ByRowPrimitiveGrantsWhateverTheRowNames`'s fixture now carries `ZM_ITEM_TM_TITANBEAM` rather than Fenna's own TM, with cross-checks that the row's item is present and Fenna's absent, so the ITEM half of 'reads off the row, not hardcoded' is proven rather than assumed -- previously it used the same TM Fenna awards and could not distinguish the two. `xZM_TRAINER_DATA_NINE_COLUMN_DEFAULTS_PROBE` plus two static_asserts in `ZM_TrainerData.h` fail the BUILD if either trailing column loses its NONE default. `ZM_Bag::Has` is total over `ZM_ITEM_NONE` (GetCount range-checks before `PocketIndexFor` reaches the asserting `ZM_GetItemData`), so NONE rows are unaffected. It is an ownership guard: the same move succeeds once the agent holds the ticket. Reproduced against BOTH the PowerShell client and the Node client, so it is board-side, not client-side. Two problems: transitions advertises the one move that by definition happens BEFORE ownership exists, and the error text describes abandonment - an unrelated failure mode - so the reader hunts for a lost claim rather than a permissions rule. Found while running /tick end-to-end for the first time; it forced that run into targeted mode instead of queue mode.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"board","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"If queueing is meant to be UI-drag-only (CLAUDE.md says \"handing work over is a drag, not a command\"), then transitions should omit \"Ready for Agent\" for a ticket the caller does not own, and move should fail with \"queueing is done on the board\" rather than an abandonment message.
