ZM-65's review returned three BLOCKING findings and all three were in material the orchestrator wrote after the gates: a stale banner still announcing a row unfrozen 50 lines above the frozen row; a new DecisionLog entry describing a source-only commit that 'moves no scene byte' in a commit that re-authored a tracked binary; and a FABRICATED causal explanation committed to two living docs (the claim that other regions' larger 12 m seam deltas arise because those pairs 'differ in flatten containment' - the terrain recipe inverts it: all three comparison pairs are identically contained, and the one pair that differs moved the LEAST). Every control points at the worker - I1 'you own the gate, the worker only authors', I2 never trust the worker, step 6.3 'review the diff' - while the orchestrator's edits are the ones no control covers: the worker has exited, gates cannot read prose, and doc_lint's seven checks never test whether a comment's assertion matches the line beneath it. And the orchestrator writes the highest-leverage text in the repo: the pin narration, the committed-asset hashes, the decision-log entry that becomes the binding record. FIX: say in step 6.3 that the review covers the WHOLE diff including orchestrator edits, and extend the existing 'grep the doc for the value you just changed' rule to every file a freeze touches, source comments included.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:37.132991","updated_at":"2026-08-24T17:20:10.021","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"rip5yck7t35h9x64uvc0r7i6","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-08-25","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"★ A SELF-REFERENTIAL GUARD PASSED EVERY GATE. The broken arm was inside a suite that ran 3415 units with 0 failures; the Zenithmon build, the D3D12 non-tools compile, the headless test suite and `doc_lint` were all green with it in place. It could not have been otherwise: the test PASSES, `doc_lint` does not read C++, and a build only proves the file compiled. Setting `fZM_GYM1_HEDGE_OPENING` to 11.75 m -- half the room's inner width, three token stubs rather than a maze -- left the entire suite green, because NOTHING in it bounded the opening from above. The per-band unit's opening clause compares `x.Min().x - innerMinX` against `fZM_GYM1_HEDGE_OPENING`, the same constant on both sides, and its only size clause is a LOWER bound. This is the guard-compared-against-a-recomputation-of-itself shape, and the only control that caught it was the independent reviewer. ★ AND THE DEFINITION OF DONE WOULD HAVE PASSED IT. The DoD asked for 'an anti-vacuity arm proving at least one wall genuinely blocks a shorter route'; arms (a)-(c) deliver exactly that and were verified non-vacuous. Arm (d) was the worker going BEYOND the DoD, and it was the broken one -- so a checkbox audit, which is what the protocol's Green-but-DoD-unmet arm inspects, reports this ticket complete. Nothing in the pipeline looks for a test that CLAIMS MORE THAN IT PROVES, and a comment asserting a guard exists is worse than no guard, because the next author reads it and stops looking. Two further instances of exactly that were found in the same file family and fixed: `ZM_Gym1Placement.h`'s solvability block attributed the opening ceiling to arm (3), which also does not bound it, and the per-band unit now carries an explicit signpost that its opening clause is a lower bound only and that the ceiling lives in the maze arm.","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/28","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"ZM-D-210's `Tests that lock it` is CORRECTED in two places, and the code it described is fixed. (1) The solvability proof's fourth anti-vacuity arm shipped BROKEN and was repaired before the commit landed. Its bound was `fMIDDLE_LIMIT = fZM_GYM1_INNER_MAX_X - fZM_GYM1_HEDGE_OPENING` -- derived from the very constant it claimed to police -- so widening the opening widened the restriction by exactly the same amount and the arm was invariant in the opening width. The bound is now `fZM_GYM1_INNER_MAX_X * 0.5f` (5.875 m, the middle half of the room), which reads only the shell. The opening width at which the arm reds is now COMPUTED -- `fREDS_AT_OPENING = innerMax - limit + playerRadius` = 6.275 m -- and asserted from both sides: it must EXCEED the authored 3.75 m (so today's layout is sealed as a geometric consequence rather than a lattice coincidence) and must sit under both half the inner width and twice the authored opening (so a materially widened opening reds). The lattice flip width (6.65 m, outermost admitted column x = +/-5.5) is computed through the search's own predicate and printed in the failure message. (2) The learnset mitigation was off by one: a level-<=5 build reaches the first TWO same-type picks (k=0, k=1), not three -- the third STAB pick is `auPicks[3]` at level 14/12/10. The mitigation stands with one index of margin. Also corrected: `ZM_MoveData.cpp`'s claim that 'a power at or below 50 would have moved them' -- at EXACTLY 50 the stable sort keeps table order, leaving Verdant Lash behind Seedshot at index 2, so the bound is STRICTLY below 50.","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"zenithmon","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"The repaired arm in `Gym1_EveryHedgeBandBlocksTheDirectRouteToTheLeader` (`Tests/ZM_Tests_Gym1Placement.cpp`). Its two meta-assertions pin `fMIDDLE_LIMIT` from both sides: loosen the strip past the gaps and the 'reds-at exceeds authored opening' clause fails; tighten it toward the centreline and the 'reds-at is under half the inner width, and under twice the authored opening' clause fails. Both existing vacuity guards are kept -- both endpoints must lie inside the restriction, and the same restriction over an EMPTY room must still succeed -- so the new bound cannot fail for the wrong reason. `ZM_GetGym1CameraSightClearanceOverFirstHedgeAtHeight(float)` was extracted so the camera anti-vacuity arm runs the SHIPPED function at a different height instead of a second copy of the interpolation, with an equality clause pinning the zero-arg accessor to it -- closing the same could-drift-silently shape one level down. Unit count UNCHANGED: no ZENITH_TEST added or removed, four assertions added inside existing units and one replaced, so the 3415 pin measured before the fix still stands and was re-confirmed by the verify phase. KNOWN AND DELIBERATE: between openings of 6.275 m and 6.65 m the meta-assertion reds while the search itself still passes -- that band says 'the seal is no longer provable, you are relying on the 0.5 m lattice', and a legitimate re-tune into it must move the bound rather than the assertion. Stated at the assertion."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T19:42:00.269803","updated_at":"2026-08-25T19:42:00.269803","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1"},{"id":"rs58e0u2sidj5cj5jmrz0wn8","values":{"fgvpu8fja84411t89jvzgvs0":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/67","h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"open","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"low","kutn19z061622yllp5eqj5ah":"zenithmon","nptzurv3ah03jchmjogdiltg":"ZM-67 residual","qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"ZM_GroundItemPropModel is total over all nine ZM_ITEM_CATEGORY values, but only ZM_ITEM_CATEGORY_BALL has its own model: MEDICINE, BATTLE, HELD, BERRY, EVO, TM, KEY and FIELD all present ZM_PROP_ITEM_PHIAL. (1) The measure phase wrote `verdict: \"all gates green\"` with `skipped: []` having run build+unit but NOT `zenith test` or `doc_lint` -- 2 of the 4 Zenithmon lines. That is correct behaviour (rule 3 measures first) but tick.md documents `skipped` as 'the gate lines that never ran' and instructs you to 'read skipped before concluding anything about what was verified'. Follow that literally at measure and you conclude a subset run was a full run. Listing deferred lines in `skipped` with reason 'deferred to verify phase' would make the field's name true again. (2) The LIVE PIN block carries TWO measured numbers and doc_lint C7 asserts both, but measure only produces one -- the registry count comes from `zenith test`, which runs in verify, AFTER the narration it feeds must be written. (2) The registry count is printed per measured game alongside the pin at :590-596 ('REGISTRY: <game> has N ZENITH_AUTOMATED_TEST_REGISTER call site(s)'), which is the second number doc_lint C7 asserts. NOTE: the deeper defect this row sat next to -- a measure phase reporting exitCode 0 / all gates green with an EMPTY steps array -- is NOT fixed by either of these and is tracked separately in the open row on that subject."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T09:41:02.686189","updated_at":"2026-08-25T09:41:02.686189","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"tby52l4w6wn6l5fn06fm45d0","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Two allowed-tools gaps in .claude/commands/tick.md that stall an unattended loop. (1) Step 5 mandates TaskStop for the wedged-worker guardrail ('If elapsed wall-clock exceeds guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes, stop the agent (TaskStop)') but TaskStop is NOT in the frontmatter allowed-tools list - so the one enforcement action for that guardrail needs a tool the skill never granted. Measured near-miss: ZM-65's worker ran 28.1 min against a 30 min MODERATE cap. The protocol's own escape hatch ('if you can see the worker still producing tool calls') is unusable because background dispatch surfaces no progress signal and tailing the subagent transcript is forbidden. (2) Step 7 mandates 'timeout 120 zagent docs sync --json' but the permission entries are Bash(zagent:*) and Bash(zagent *), both anchored on zagent as the FIRST token - 'timeout 120 zagent ...' matches neither. The fix for the hang moved the command out from under its own permission entry, at the one step that stalls AFTER the commit lands and BEFORE finish. Better fix: give 'zagent docs sync' a --timeout-seconds flag so the bounded call stays a bare zagent invocation. Note the hang itself reproduced again on ZM-65: exit 143, zero-byte log - four ticks, four hangs.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Both gaps closed. (1) TaskStop is in tick.md's frontmatter allowed-tools (tick.md:3), so the wedged-worker guardrail's one enforcement action is granted. (2) The 'timeout 120 zagent docs sync --json' mandate is gone -- step 7 calls it bare at tick.md:1726 -- so the command no longer falls outside its own first-token-anchored permission entry. The hang it worked around was root-caused upstream (05408ef: a WebSocket per page for all 597 pages) and tick.md:1729-1738 now records it as fixed history rather than a live hazard. The first-token anchoring of Bash(zagent *) in .claude/settings.json:8-9 is unchanged and still real; it is documented as a trap at tick.md:121-124, which is why the wrapper was removed rather than the allowlist widened."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:36.102968","updated_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:36.102968","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"u7vnutexpqldfxrnqsj3icqs","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"AUDIT WRAP-UP 2026-08-24: what landed in the Zenith checkout, and the four halves that are BOARD-SIDE and still open. Landed here across ae475483 (tick.md + settings.json) and 39b24437 (Tools/zagent, +12 assertions, 158 total, smoked against the real board): the refused-claim rollback, the drift resolver's category ranking, the finish --status Done DoD refusal, client UTF-8 output, TaskStop and Bash(timeout *) in allowed-tools, rulings added to I3's inline list, the windowed-authoring correction plus a nine-step needs-gpu runbook, step 6's total ordering, step 7's third arm, the three orchestrator-owned measurements, reconciliation against code rather than comments, a file-list derivation rule, and I2 widened to distrust 'it cannot be done' as well as 'it works'. STILL BOARD-SIDE, in priority order: (1) zagent claim should VALIDATE BEFORE IT MUTATES -- the client now rolls a refused claim back, but that is a bandage over a transaction that writes then checks, and 'zagent check' already evaluates needsHuman and EPIC without writing, so the same gate can run before the transaction; (2) 'zagent docs sync' HANGS -- four ticks, four hangs, four zero-byte logs, most recently exit 143 on ZM-65 -- and wants a --timeout-seconds flag so the bounded call stays a bare zagent invocation rather than needing a generic process wrapper on the allowlist; (3) review.required should gain a third OR term, 'the ticket's subject matter is governed by a recorded decision', computable from the decisionLog that zagent.project.json already declares -- ZM-23 was reviewed only by the luck of MEDIUM sitting in reviewOn, and that review is the only thing that caught it violating ZM-D-203 Ruling 3; (4) the claim payload could resolve candidate rulings into .zagent/run/<KEY>/rulings.md the way it already writes drift.txt, which turns I3's new rulings clause from prose into a file the orchestrator cannot fail to see. Also note guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes looks mis-tiered against measurement: the one observed MODERATE run used 94 percent of its 30-minute budget while both COMPLEX runs used about 16 percent of 90.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"All four board-side halves now closed, three by this pass. (1) claim validates BEFORE it mutates -- already fixed before triage: executeOperation runs prepare() and only then builds changes and commits, so the old write-then-rollback bandage is gone and claim-refusal-atomicity.test.mjs pins it. (2) docs sync --timeout-seconds is MOOT, not done: docs sync no longer exists in the read-only local vault, and the hang it would have bounded was root-caused upstream (a WebSocket per page for all 597) -- the stale CLAUDE.md and tick.md rows describing it were deleted in this same pass. (3) review.required gained the third OR term, governed-by-a-recorded-decision, in cli/legacy-pure/ticket.mjs, wired through compat.mjs reviewOf so it actually fires (it was inert on first landing) and verified against real tickets on the real binary. (4) the claim payload now writes .zagent/run/<KEY>/rulings.md alongside drift.txt, and writes it even when the category declares no decision log, saying so -- an empty file and a missing one read identically to a worker. On the guardrail note: ticketTimeoutMinutes is still TRIVIAL/SIMPLE 15, MODERATE 30, COMPLEX 90, unchanged, so the mis-tiering this row observed stands and is NOT addressed here."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T17:20:30.417789","updated_at":"2026-08-24T17:20:30.417789","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"udgwpd6xkjtg6qzhxfih41xt","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Both halves are now closed. The board half landed in the previous board's 9d03869 (2026-08-25): parseTicket carries continuation lines, so definitionOfDone[].text is no longer truncated at the first newline -- verified against ZM-23, the ticket that exposed it. The tick.md half is stated and STILL STANDS, but on a reason that never depended on the bug: the array holds the checkboxes and never the prose that qualifies them, and ZM-23's body carried two load-bearing instructions OUTSIDE any checkbox. So 'inline from body.md, never from the array' is a rule about what the array IS, not a workaround. The worked example of what the truncation cost -- including that the reachability scan could not see a protectedPath written on a continuation line -- moved to Docs/TickProtocolHistory.md, since it is now history rather than a live hazard. Zenith e411b451.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"The payload's definitionOfDone[].text truncates each checkbox at its first newline. On ZM-23 that deletes the entire substance of two items: item 1 loses 'not bumped to a larger count ... caught as a DOUBLE CLAIM on ZM_TRAINER_RIVAL_VESPER, proven by an anti-vacuity arm' (the whole point of the ticket), and item 3 loses 'are REPORTED from the shipped tables rather than asserted' (the clause preventing a self-referential guard). I3 makes the DoD the worker's verbatim specification, and the array is the obvious thing to inline because it is structured and already in the payload. A tick that does so ships a mutilated spec, and the worker cannot tell, having no shell and no board. It also weakens finish --status Done's unticked-box refusal, which reads the same truncated text.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"contract","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"blocks-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Preserve the FULL text of every Definition-of-Done checkbox in the claim payload, including continuation lines. Until then, tick.md step 5 must say explicitly: inline the DoD from body.md, never from the definitionOfDone array.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T00:34:09.250173","updated_at":"2026-08-26T10:50:08.1","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"uwmovps6f4vcy8ojoeltamis","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"tick.md spends ~40 lines and three measured war stories on 'NEVER PIPE OR SUFFIX A CALL WHOSE EXIT CODE YOU INTEND TO READ', and it is still the most-broken rule in the protocol. It broke twice more on 2026-08-25: I ran `zagent check ZM-70 2>&1 | head -20; echo EXIT=$?` and read 0 when the real code was 5, within the hour of reading the warning; and the harness's own completion notification reported exit 0 for a tick_gates run that exited 10 (MEASURED: a pin needs bumping) -- branching on that commits a stale baseline. The asymmetry is the whole point: EVERY other value the protocol says to read from a file IS on disk (ticket.json, body.md, drift.txt, gates.json, tick_gates.json) precisely because pipes corrupt them, and the exit code -- the single most-warned-about value -- is reachable ONLY through the channel the protocol says never to trust. .zagent/last.json carries the ticket payload and no exit code; nothing writes a last.exit. tick_gates.ps1 already solved this for itself with tick_gates.json, which is why its verdict survived while the shell's did not. FIX: zagent.ps1 ends in `exit $result.exitCode` (:356) with 8 earlier exit paths (:82,:91,:125,:129,:133,:148,:181,:223). Wrap them in one Exit-Zagent function that writes the code to .zagent/last.exit and then exits, and assert it in Test-ZagentClient.ps1. Two lines of real change, and it deletes the entire error class rather than warning about it -- which matters because the protocol's own history says the warning does not hold.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"blocks-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Write zagent's exit code to .zagent/last.exit on every exit path, so the protocol's most-broken rule becomes a file read like every other rule.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-26","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Implemented, with the mechanism in Node rather than PowerShell. Tools/zagent/zagent.ps1 is now a 65-line dispatch shim with no exit paths of its own, so the cited line numbers are gone; the persistence moved to Tools/Vault/cli/client.mjs:355-358 persistLast, which always writes .zagent/last.exit, invoked from the single choke point finish() at client.mjs:496-513 that every return in runClient funnels through. The comment at client.mjs:487-491 states the invariant the row asked for -- a return that bypasses it is exactly the defect this exists to remove -- and markRunning() (client.mjs:388-395) invalidates the slot up front so a crashed run cannot leave a stale code readable. Asserted in client.test.mjs, tick-checks.test.mjs and write-integration.test.mjs."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-26T00:37:32.535357","updated_at":"2026-08-26T00:37:32.535357","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"vnfymz4lx659r5jwrzo5rwdg","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed in Tools/zagent/ZagentClient.psm1 (39b24437). Verified live: ZM-30's Status.md and Shortfalls.md now resolve to Games/Zenithmon/ where they previously resolved to DevilsPlayground. +5 assertions.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"The drift resolver names the WRONG GAME's file whenever two games share a filename, and it is deterministic rather than occasional. Measured across four ZM tickets: Roadmap.md and Board.md exist only under Games/Zenithmon, so the resolver suggests the Zenithmon path and is right BY LUCK; Status.md and Shortfalls.md exist under BOTH Zenithmon and DevilsPlayground, and the resolver suggested the DevilsPlayground path every time (ZM-23, ZM-30 x2). It walks in path order and takes the first match, and DevilsPlayground sorts before Zenithmon. It then presents that single pick as an answer - 'a file of that name is at X' - with no sign a second candidate exists, while tick.md step 5 tells the orchestrator to reconcile drift.txt and correct the worker prompt from it. So it is right exactly when there is no ambiguity and wrong exactly when the hint would have carried information. FIX: rank candidates by the ticket's category paths prefix, and when more than one survives print them ALL - a list reads as a question, one path reads as an answer.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-24","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T16:53:36.609676","updated_at":"2026-08-24T17:20:10.535","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"vqcx8n38dyainq08yrrpz4dn","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"ZEN-6's DoD item 4 read 'the headless publish guard is removed, and the reasoning is recorded in the decision log' -- and the claim payload came back with `decisionLog: null` and `decisionIdPrefix: null`, because only the Zenithmon and DevilsPlayground categories declare one. So an Engine ticket that asks for a recorded ruling has no repo-local decision log to record it in, and `zagent decide --ticket ZEN-6` writes the board's Decisions database only. That matters more than it sounds: I3 tells every tick to GREP the decision log for the rulings that govern its subject, and a loop worker has no shell and no network -- it reads the file off disk. An engine ruling recorded only on the board is invisible to exactly the audience I3 exists to serve, and ZEN-6's ruling is one every future scene-authoring ticket needs (it is what makes `needs-gpu` wrong for scene re-authoring). I worked around it by narrating the Zenithmon-visible half into Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md, which is where a ZM tick greps -- but that is the wrong home for an ENGINE decision and it only reaches ZM. Options: (a) declare a decisionLog for Engine, e.g. Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md with prefix ZEN-D-; (b) let a category with no decisionLog inherit a project-level one; (c) at minimum, have `zagent decide` WARN when the ticket's category declares no decisionLog, so the tick notices instead of silently getting a board-only row. Right now the omission is silent -- `decide` returns exit 0 and says 'Wrote a row to Agent - Decisions', which reads exactly like success.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"config","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Give the Engine category a `decisionLog` in zagent.project.json, or make the project-level decisionLog a fallback for categories that declare none.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-26","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed together with the paired row filed on ZEN-19. Option (c) from this row was ALSO taken: zagent decide now warns when the ticket category declares no decisionLog, naming the category and saying the row will exist only on the board where a worker resolving rulings from disk will never see it. Exit code is unchanged, so it informs without refusing. Option (b), a project-level inherited default, was deliberately NOT taken -- the other categories file on different board projects, so one shared prefix would misattribute their rulings."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-26T12:18:43.626737","updated_at":"2026-08-26T12:18:43.626737","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"wltdr0zcbl79npl4cdr80vou","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-08-25","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"★ THE DURABLE FINDING, and it is the reason this entry exists rather than a work-log line: APPENDING A MOVE IS NEVER INERT. `ZM_MoveData` is not a lookup table -- it has two DERIVED consumers that scan the whole of it. `Source/Data/ZM_Learnsets.cpp:52` (`ZM_GetSpeciesLearnset`) rebuilds every species' level-up list by partitioning the entire move table by type and sorting the damaging buckets with `SortByEffectivePower`, a stable insertion sort ASCENDING on raw power; and `Source/Data/ZM_SpeciesData.cpp:555` (`ZM_GetSpeciesEggMoves`) scans the table again in table order for type matches not already in the learnset, capped at 6. So one appended GRASS move re-sorts every GRASS species' learnset, which propagates into `ZM_BuildWildEnemySpec`, `ZM_BuildMonsterRecord`, breeding and the battle tower. NO BLAST-RADIUS GREP FINDS THIS -- the coupling is by table scan, not by identifier, so a file-list survey over the changed symbols comes back clean. It was found only because the worker read the consumers. SEVEN MORE GYM REWARD MOVES REMAIN, so this recurs seven times unless it is written down. Mitigation taken here: Verdant Lash is 65 power, which sorts strictly ABOVE the shipped Leafcut (55) and therefore lands at sorted index >= 3 in the GRASS bucket -- the first three same-type picks are the only ones a level-<=5 build reaches, so the L5 starter and every Route 1 encounter are unaffected; deeper GRASS learnsets shift by one entry. That relationship is asserted as a COMPARISON against the shipped Leafcut row rather than as a literal 65, so it survives a re-tune of either move. Verified against the code at both cited sites, not against their comments. Secondary finding, same shape: `ZM_ITEM_ID` groups TMs in the MIDDLE of the enum, before the key items, and `ZM_SaveSchema` writes bag item ids as raw uint16 -- so filing the new TM with its siblings would have renumbered six key items and invalidated every existing save. It is appended at the true end after `ZM_ITEM_EGGVOUCHER`; `ZM_MOVE_ID` is grouped by type and got the same treatment. Scope context: badge STATE and the teach-move MECHANISM both already existed (ZM-D-209 item 4), so this slice adds rows and indices, never systems.","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/28","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"ZM-28 (G1-1) lands Gym 1's pure half: `ZM_Gym1Placement.h` declares a 24x20 m interior hall whose maze is three full-width hedge bands with a single opening each, alternating sides (a serpentine), and ships the walkability predicate the tests and the future authoring both read rather than re-deriving geometry. `ZM_BadgeData.{h,cpp}` carries the eight GDD badge indices and names in the ZM-D-009 compiled-const-table idiom, with a static_assert tying its width to the EXISTING `uZM_BADGE_COUNT` rather than restating it -- no badge state, no save-schema change. Fenna is `ZM_TRAINER_GYM1_FENNA`: 3 GRASS monsters at the GDD's level 13, prize 2600, `ZM_AI_TIER_SMART`, defeat flag the ALREADY-REGISTERED `ZM_STORY_FLAG_GYM1_DEFEATED`. Verdant Lash lands as both `ZM_MOVE_VERDANTLASH` and `ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH`. Fenna is authored at IDENTITY rotation and the room is shaped so that is correct -- identity forward is +Z, she stands at z=-7.0 and the arrival is at z=+7.0, so she already faces the player, which sidesteps ProfLab's frozen-half-turn problem BY PLACEMENT and lets her legally wear an AABB collider (ZM-D-193). This slice AUTHORS NOTHING: no .zscen byte moved.","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"zenithmon","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"hard","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"New `Tests/ZM_Tests_Gym1Placement.cpp` (13 boot units). Solvability is a 4-connected BFS over a 47x39 lattice at the shipped body radius, with three anti-vacuity arms rather than one: (a) the empty-room baseline must equal the EXACT straight-line cell count, so the search is known sound before it is trusted; (b) the maze route must be strictly longer than that baseline; (c) every band must block the arrival->leader centreline AND be shown to be the one blocking it (removing just that band unblocks that point); and the strongest arm -- restricting the walk to the middle of the room must make the maze UNSOLVABLE while both endpoints stay inside the restriction, which is what reds if someone widens an opening toward the centre. `ZM_GetGym1CameraSightClearanceOverFirstHedge()` measures the 2.0 m hedge against the 3.9 m settled camera (~0.59 m) with an anti-vacuity arm feeding the shell's own 4.0 m wall height through identical arithmetic and requiring it to FAIL. `Gym1_LeaderFacesTheArrivalAtIdentity` checks the identity-rotation claim through the shipped `ZM_ForwardFromRotation` rather than by restating the axis. `Fenna_AuthoredValuesAreExact` in `ZM_Tests_TrainerData.cpp` pins her row. Three pinned counts moved with the data -- `uEXPECTED_TRAINERS` 2->3, `uEXPECTED_ITEMS` 90->91, `uEXPECTED_MOVES` 218->219 -- each spelled in its TEST rather than read off the table, so a roster change is a failure and not a tautology. Gate: regen (both new .cpp files detected and compiled), Zenithmon --headless build, the D3D12 non-tools compile, `zenith test Zenithmon --headless`, and the boot unit gate OBSERVED at 3415 ran / 3413 passed / 0 failed, moving `Tools/unit_baselines.json` 3401 -> 3415. Registry unchanged at 70."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T19:12:33.08069","updated_at":"2026-08-25T19:12:33.08069","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1"},{"id":"wmbefyl4qdqe3wziv93q2eg2","values":{"o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"zagent already refuses a DoD naming a protectedPath. One rg for ZM_TRAINER_ROUTE1_RAMBLER would have surfaced Tests/ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp before the claim, the one-ticket-per-repo lock slot and two opus worker dispatches. Raised by the ZM-23 worker itself.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"contract","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"At file time, grep the repo for the identifiers a Definition of Done proposes to change and warn when hits land outside the ticket's declared file list.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-25","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Implemented as a warning at create time, never a refusal, as the row asked. write.mjs dodBlastRadiusWarning extracts the code identifiers a Definition of Done proposes to change, greps the repo and warns when hits land outside the declared file list (derived from the existing citation parser). Kept deliberately cheap so create stays snappy: at most 8 identifiers in first-appearance order, ONE git grep carrying them all as OR-ed patterns rather than a process per identifier, a 5s timeout, 20 files reported. Any failure -- no repo, timeout, no matches -- is silent by design, since a noisy warning is one people learn to skip. This sits beside the existing protected-path reachability scan, which answers a different question: that one asks whether a DoD NAMES a protected path, this asks whether its blast radius exceeds what it declared."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T00:34:09.779686","updated_at":"2026-08-25T00:34:09.779686","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"wni6bvf0tegsslnu6ubuoim1","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Shipped: contract validation scans the Definition of Done for the effective protectedPaths union and refuses at FILE time (board.ts:1091), so a ticket no agent could finish never costs a claim. The cheaper label alternative it offered was not needed.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Two consecutive tickets carried a Definition-of-Done item the loop provably cannot satisfy, and `contractValid` was true for both. ZM-54 requires \"a Zenithmon invocation runs in CI\" -- that is .github/workflows/doc-lint.yml, protected, so zagent guard refuses it. ZM-50's class requires bumping a pinned unit baseline, which for Zenithmon lives in three files of which .github/workflows/zm-tests.yml and zagent.project.json are both protected. In both cases the loop claimed the ticket, spent time reading the repo, and only then discovered the work was unreachable. Contract validation currently checks routing, category, complexity and risk -- whether the ticket can be ROUTED -- but not whether what it asks for can be DONE by an agent bound by protectedPaths. The board already has the concept and the machinery: `windowed` keeps work that needs a human at a keyboard out of the claim query entirely, and a targeted claim on one fails the contract by name.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"contract","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Extend contract validation to scan the Definition of Done (and ideally the Goal) for paths matching the effective protectedPaths union, and fail at FILE time the way a missing --category already does -- refusing only when filing straight into Ready for Agent, warning when filing into To Do, matching the existing behaviour. A DoD line naming .github/**, zagent.project.json or .claude/** is a ticket no agent can finish, and finding that out at claim time wastes a claim, a slot in the one-ticket-per-repo lock, and whatever model time the worker burns before someone notices. If static path detection is too brittle, the cheaper version is a `human-only` label that behaves exactly like `windowed`: filtered from the queue, contract-invalid on a targeted claim.","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/54","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-21","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-21T02:34:51.352571","updated_at":"2026-08-23T20:54:24.803","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"xvlghsuxnrv05euj5ee1bs7s","values":{"dnzedm3e8obk7b1b7bjpti6e":"Apply ruling §2.2's disposition unchanged: keep the FLAGGED half (uFlaggedRows > 0 plus the Vesper fixture pin), and RETIRE the flagless half in the file with its reason recorded there, stating that the flagless arm is deliberately fixture-only from here because a flagless registered row IS the farmable-prize state. Then move the anti-vacuity guard to where it now belongs — assert that the hand-built fixture the re-pointed Gate_Flagless* unit uses really does carry ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE, so the fixture cannot silently gain a flag either. That preserves the guard's purpose at the new seam instead of deleting it.","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"What replaces the FLAGLESS half of Gate_ShippedRosterStillExercisesBothArms (ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp:2275) once Ruling 3 forbids any registered row being flagless?","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"open","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"medium","osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-08-25","x8xpkuruebvskqi2lckjm1o7":"The unit is a roster ANTI-VACUITY guard: it asserts uFlaggedRows > 0 and uFlaglessRows > 0 over the shipped roster, then pins the two named fixtures individually (Vesper flagged at :2307, Rambler flagless at :2310). Its entire flagless premise is what ZM-D-196 Ruling 3 retires. Its own failure message instructs a future implementer to \"point the flagless one at a row that really has no flag\" — which ZM-D-208 §2.2 forbids in bold (\"Do NOT keep some row flagless to preserve the phase\"). So the file's own guidance becomes unsatisfiable, and the two options are the same two ruling §2.2 already weighed for phase 8. This is the ONLY thing blocking ZM-23; the other two Gate_* units are mechanical under ruling §2.1's own words. Note this is a coverage judgement, not a mechanical fix, which is why neither the worker nor the orchestrator made it.","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"zenithmon"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-25T00:33:44.829109","updated_at":"2026-08-25T00:33:44.829109","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor"},{"id":"yq41hev2uelvu576mw3dfr70","values":{"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Shipped in the previous board's dc80c1e. `recordTransition` is now the one writer of jira.issue_activity for both status and assignee, and `recordClaim` is a caller of it rather than a parallel implementation; `moveTicket` and `finishTicket` both record their move. `planAgentMove` returns the from-status and from-assignee it had already loaded, so no caller re-reads the row. moveTicket became a transaction where it was a bare UPDATE, so the move and its history row land together. `zagent history <KEY>` now shows To Do -> In Progress -> Done in order, which is asserted as a SEQUENCE (a test that only checked \"some row mentions Done\" would pass on a trail with the moves backwards).","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Reconstructing what happened to a ticket means reading the org activity feed and correlating by timestamp, rather than reading the ticket's own history. The gap was invisible for as long as nothing wrote the claim either -- `history` on a freshly claimed ticket said 'No recorded changes', so the whole table looked unused rather than half-used.","ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"board","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"nuisance","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Record `move` and `finish` in jira.issue_activity, the way `claim` now does. `updateTicket` was the only writer of that table, so the ticket LIFECYCLE left no per-issue trail at all: a claim wrote nothing (fixed), and moveTicket/finishTicket still write only the org-wide activity feed (recordActivity), which is a different table with a different shape. The helper is already there -- packages/agent/src/board.ts `recordClaim` -- and both call sites already know the from/to status, so this is a few lines each. Until then `zagent history <KEY>` shows a ticket being claimed and never being closed, which reads as an in-flight ticket that nobody finished.","wgtve3zh07arsflze8hn5icw":"2026-08-23","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-23T11:11:29.577391","updated_at":"2026-08-23T21:17:39.051","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8"},{"id":"z3qzphquongyre1acm3s0sdj","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-08-26","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"The guard treated a symptom. Its stated reason was correct -- a Null tools boot authored an INCOMPLETE world, and serializing that subset over a tracked asset once dropped RenderTest's two instanced-tree entities, ~323 KB of a 361,753-byte file, on every headless boot, with a dirty `git status` as the only symptom. But the incompleteness had a single cause: an authoring step that needed a live GPU resource bailed out ENTIRELY instead of skipping only the GPU part. That bail conflated two different things -- creating the entities and their components, which is SCENE DATA and exactly what `WriteToDataStream` serializes, against allocating the GPU buffers, which is not serialized at all. The decisive evidence is that a headless boot ALREADY ran the whole chain verbatim -- `LoadMesh -> EnsureInstanceGroupCreated -> Reserve -> InitialiseGPUBuffers -> SpawnInstanceWithMatrix` -- every time `Zenith_InstancedMeshComponent::ReadFromDataStream` loaded the committed scene's 2,520 tree instances. The authoring path and the load path differed only in that one bail, so there was never a GPU allocation to skip; the branch skipped the scene data instead. ★ THE COST THIS REMOVES: eight Zenithmon tickets carried `needs-gpu` for no reason other than that they re-author a committed scene, and six of the ten tickets on the S8 critical path sat behind one, so the chain alternated human and agent work and the loop could never get more than one ticket ahead of a keyboard session. ★ AND WHAT REPLACES THE GUARD AS PROTECTION IS A TEST, NOT A POLICY: `Editor.TreeAuthoringIsBackendNeutral` asserts the canonical authoring step produces its two entities BY NAME, each carrying the component and each non-transient, on whichever backend is running -- so a re-introduced Null bail reddens a unit instead of silently shrinking a tracked asset. `RT_SceneAssetIntegrity` becomes the end-to-end half: its assertions are unchanged, but they were near-vacuous headless (a headless boot never wrote the file) and are now real.","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZEN/issue/6","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"The headless `.zscen` publish guard in `Zenith_Editor::SaveActiveScene` is REMOVED, because its cause was fixed rather than tolerated. `Zenith_TerrainEditor::EnsureTreeEntities` no longer returns false on its first line under `Zenith_IsNullRenderer()`: it creates `TerrainTrees_Trunk` and `TerrainTrees_Leaves` and their `Zenith_InstancedMeshComponent`s on every backend. No replacement branch was needed for the GPU half, because `Flux_InstanceGroup::InitialiseGPUBuffers` on the Null backend is already `Zenith_Null_MemoryManager` handing back dummy handles -- the backend supplies the skip. `Zenith_SceneData::CompareWithFile` and `Zenith_ScenePublishDelta` SURVIVE the removal, promoted from guard to audit and applied on every backend: `AuditScenePublish` logs `[ScenePublish] CREATED|IDENTICAL|CHANGED`, still skips a byte-identical write, and still reports a publish that drops entities as a `Zenith_Error` -- it no longer REFUSES, because deleting an entity is a legitimate authoring change, but the original defect's exact shape does not pass in silence. `EnsureTreeEntities` and the two entity-name constants are now public seams so a unit can pin them without driving a brush stroke.","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"hard","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"OBSERVED, not asserted. A `Null_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` boot driven with `--automated-test <T> --skip-unit-tests` re-authored every committed scene both games publish and reported `[ScenePublish] IDENTICAL` for all five: RenderTest at 82 entities / 361,753 bytes (byte-for-byte the committed file, trees included), and Zenithmon's FrontEnd, PlayerHome, Battle and ProfLab. Zero `CHANGED` verdicts; `git status` clean afterwards. ★ THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THAT PROOF WAS WORTHLESS AND LOOKED EXACTLY LIKE SUCCESS: the unit-gate boot exits before the editor-automation queue drains, so it authors nothing, emits no scene marker and leaves a clean tree. A clean tree is the fail-open state here, and the proof requires an authoring boot plus the marker. Units: `Editor.HeadlessSaveNeverRewritesSceneAsset` (which pinned the removed policy, and carried its own `if constexpr` Null branch) is replaced by `Editor.ScenePublishWritesOnEveryBackend`, which asserts the same property on BOTH backends and so needs no branch; `Editor.TreeAuthoringIsBackendNeutral` is new; `SceneSaveDeltaClassifiesPublish` is untouched and still pins all three delta results. Net +1 unit, BACKEND-NEUTRAL, so every game's row moved and ALL THREE WERE MEASURED: Combat 1650->1651, Zenithmon 3419->3420, Null RenderTest 1741->1742. Gates: all 8 Engine builds green (every game compiles), Combat suite and unit gate green, and the full audit of all ten `Zenith_IsNullRenderer()` sites recorded -- three removed, five in `Zenith/Editor/` confirmed correct as written, two in `Flux/Vegetation` correct (they create no entity), one being the constexpr definition itself."},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-26T11:27:01.539088","updated_at":"2026-08-26T11:27:01.539088","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1"},{"id":"zh9ou77182krefhzr6z6jjci","values":{"dnzedm3e8obk7b1b7bjpti6e":"Option (a): add a by-ROW overload ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool) and re-point ZM_Tests_Party.cpp at it, keeping the coverage at the cost of a little production surface. Option (b) - retire the unit and phase 8 with a recorded reason - is cheaper but deletes the only end-to-end proof that the NONE arm pays and does not raise, and ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE remains live production code. Note also that Ruling 3's own reasoning is slightly off on mechanism: ZM_BattleWriteBack.h:101-104 records that a second win credits the money AGAIN ('pay once' is a caller-side gate), so the flag does not stop farming by itself - it stops it because ZM_MayTrainerEngage refuses to raise a defeated flagged trainer. The flag's value is real but is delivered through the sight FSM, not the payout helper.","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"http://localhost:3001/pink-goat/project/ZM/issue/23","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"Ruling 3 says the flagless arm 'must stay covered by the existing test-only reconfiguration', but that remedy only reaches ONE of the three flagless-arm consumers. What happens to the other two?","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"resolved","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"medium","osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-08-24","pfp140d5cgrhvbsth95eskme":"RULED: option (a), extended to name phase 8's disposition -- (a) as filed covers ZM_Tests_Party.cpp only and is silent on the third consumer, which is where the implementer would otherwise hit the same wall. THREE PARTS. (1) Add the by-ROW primitive ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool) and re-point ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099 at it. This is an EXTRACTION, not new logic: the by-id function already resolves the row at ZM_BattleWriteBack.cpp:133 and works purely from it thereafter, so by-id becomes classify + ZM_IsRegisteredTrainer + resolve + forward, mirroring how the ZM_BattleDirectorCore overload already forwards. Coverage is strengthened, not merely preserved -- a hand-built row cannot drift when content changes. (2) RETIRE phase 8 of ZM_AutoTests_TrainerSight.cpp, with the reason recorded IN THE TEST FILE: its precondition is a flagless REGISTERED trainer row, and Ruling 3 makes that state deliberately unreachable, so the phase would be proving the behaviour of a configuration production can no longer produce. Do NOT keep some row flagless to preserve the phase -- that is the farmable-prize state Ruling 3 exists to forbid, and preserving a test by preserving the defect it warns about is the wrong trade. (3) Do NOT give ZM_Interactable::ConfigureTrainerSight a by-row overload. It stores m_eTrainerId and re-derives it in OnStart from the serialized NPC row (the deliberate zero-byte route); a by-row configure would need somewhere to put a row outside the registry and would fight that design. WHAT SURVIVES: ZM_MayTrainerEngage's flagless/latch arm by row in ZM_Tests_IntroBeat.cpp:176 with an anti-vacuity arm; the FSM latch in ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp; the write-back NONE arm by row in ZM_Tests_Party.cpp. WHAT IS GENUINELY LOST: the live-component end-to-end proof that a flagless row pays and does not raise. That is a real cost, recorded rather than waved away. ALSO CARRY FORWARD the question's correction to Ruling 3's stated mechanism: the flag does NOT stop farming through the payout helper -- ZM_BattleWriteBack.h:101-104 records that a second win credits the money AGAIN, since 'pay once' is a caller-side gate -- it stops it because ZM_MayTrainerEngage refuses to raise a defeated flagged trainer. The flag's value is real but is delivered through the sight FSM, not the payout helper.","x8xpkuruebvskqi2lckjm1o7":"Flagging both Route 1 trainers (Ruling 3, DecisionLog.md:912) retires ZM_TRAINER_ROUTE1_RAMBLER as the only flagless PRODUCTION row. Three consumers exercise the ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE arm, and they split two ways. ZM_MayTrainerEngage(const ZM_TrainerData&, ...) (ZM_TrainerSightFsm.h:315) takes a ROW, so its units can use a test-local fixture - this is the case the ruling's remedy covers. But ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState takes a ZM_TRAINER_ID (ZM_BattleWriteBack.h:105 and :112 - BOTH overloads are by-id, verified), and ZM_Interactable::ConfigureTrainerSight(ZM_TRAINER_ID) likewise. No hand-built row can reach either. Once every registered row is flagged the only flagless ids are UNREGISTERED ones, which are a total silent no-op and therefore cannot exercise 'pays money but writes no flag'. Affected coverage: ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099 TrainerReward_UnflaggedRowStillPaysAndWritesNoFlag (3 assertions) and phase (8) of ZM_AutoTests_TrainerSight.cpp (:140, :3024).","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"zenithmon"},"page_id":null,"created_at":"2026-08-24T14:45:25.139015","updated_at":"2026-08-24T21:49:07.356","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor"},{"id":"320d696d-50d9-4f58-80a3-d3815be9d2cc","database_id":"gm1dzh0b1o8u1p38sosvoco4","values":{"bih0nae73jl5qkv6uih6task":"ZEN-D-001","bjs5nsf3nkc4eea6d4kvfrli":"A Zenith_AssertCaptureScope test MUST read the hit count into a local INSIDE the scope and assert on it OUTSIDE. Asserting the count inside the scope is FAIL-OPEN, and that is the shape most existing capture tests in this repo currently use.","bp9jeufcanmqiblw7pq8ax8q":"c-dev-zenith","dm4mxfvxv5eug34ch759t5ra":"ZEN-7","hns5iycp45kq5mllb4zat8zx":"Core::AssertEqFloatFailsOnNaN and Core::AssertNearVec3FailsOnNaN (Zenith/Core/Zenith_UnitTests.Tests.inl) demonstrate the correct shape -- ten capture scopes, each reading GetHitCount() as the last statement inside the block. Nothing yet ENFORCES the shape across the repo; that is the open follow-up.","m60k4ui1qewy9tu9u5u1edvb":"Zenith_TestRunner::HandleFailure (Zenith/Core/Zenith_TestFramework.cpp:209-219) returns early for EVERY framework assertion while g_bAssertCaptureActive is set -- it increments the counter and returns before m_bCurrentTestFailed is set. So a ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ on GetHitCount() written inside the scope is itself swallowed: when the count is wrong the assertion records nothing and the test PASSES. The capture mechanism cannot distinguish the assertion under test from the assertion checking it. Verified against Zenith/UnitTests/Zenith_AssertCapture.cpp: the ctor zeroes the counter and the dtor restores the previous value, so per-scope counts are isolated and reading inside / asserting outside is correct and cheap (one local). Zenith/AI/Navigation/Zenith_NavMesh.Tests.inl (~lines 620-850) asserts INSIDE and is the convention ZEN-7's worker was pointed at as the worked example; it is affected. Found by the ZEN-7 worker while writing the two new units, which use the correct shape. Sweeping the existing capture tests onto it is a separate diff across many test files and was deliberately left out of ZEN-7.","vl51anabw4bazm7tvt72na7h":"easy","zjr55or91hidtu1kp33iu7vx":"Testing","zp5jckpmecaw3p49w2bbzzfh":"2026-09-19"},"created_at":"2026-09-19T20:36:01.545Z","updated_at":"2026-09-19T20:36:01.545Z"},{"id":"4155bc1d-c06f-48d5-8647-ad54bcc36b36","database_id":"gm1dzh0b1o8u1p38sosvoco4","values":{"bih0nae73jl5qkv6uih6task":"ZEN-D-002","bjs5nsf3nkc4eea6d4kvfrli":"ZENITH_ASSERT_NE is left FAIL-OPEN on NaN, deliberately, and the reason is recorded at the macro in Zenith/Core/Zenith_TestFramework.h. It is the ONE comparison assertion of the six that does not fail closed on a degenerate float. Do not reach for NE to prove a float is healthy.","bp9jeufcanmqiblw7pq8ax8q":"c-dev-zenith","dm4mxfvxv5eug34ch759t5ra":"ZEN-7","hns5iycp45kq5mllb4zat8zx":"NOTHING. This is a documented non-fix: no test pins ZENITH_ASSERT_NE's NaN behaviour in either direction, and a future change to its spelling would not red anything. The lock is the comment at Zenith/Core/Zenith_TestFramework.h above the macro block.","m60k4ui1qewy9tu9u5u1edvb":"The six template comparisons are generated by ZENITH_DEFINE_COMPARE_ASSERT, which takes the condition under which the assertion FAILS. Five are spelled as the negation of the relation they assert -- Eq is !(a == b), Gt is !(a > b), and so on -- and since every comparison against a NaN is false, the negation is true and the assertion fails. That is why ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ on two NaNs already FAILS. ZENITH_ASSERT_NE is spelled (a == b), NOT a negation, so it fails only when the operands are EQUAL -- and a NaN equals nothing. ZENITH_ASSERT_NE(fSpeed, 0.0f) therefore PASSES when fSpeed is NaN. That is literally correct (a NaN is indeed not zero) and is almost never what the author meant, which is usually 'this is a real number and it is not zero'. Tightening it would change the MEANING of the assertion rather than close a hole in it, so it is left alone and documented instead. Surfaced by the ZEN-7 reviewer: the worker's survivor comment declared all six survivors on the grounds that EQ fails on NaN, which is true but covers only the five that fail closed and was silent about the one that does not. ZEN-7's DoD required each survivor be recorded WITH A REASON, so the comment was corrected rather than left overclaiming. Related: a NaN passed as the EPSILON also makes any finite comparison pass, because fabs(a - b) > NaN is false. Epsilons are near-always literals, so that is a remark rather than a known defect, and it is noted at the same macro.","vl51anabw4bazm7tvt72na7h":"easy","zjr55or91hidtu1kp33iu7vx":"Testing","zp5jckpmecaw3p49w2bbzzfh":"2026-09-19"},"created_at":"2026-09-19T20:36:06.943Z","updated_at":"2026-09-19T20:36:06.943Z"},{"id":"c0121771-aaaf-4317-931a-6bad62122ff8","database_id":"gm1dzh0b1o8u1p38sosvoco4","values":{"bih0nae73jl5qkv6uih6task":"ZEN-D-003","bjs5nsf3nkc4eea6d4kvfrli":"A `ZENITH_AUTOMATED_TEST_REGISTER` harness test in `Games/RenderTest/Tests/**` is COMPILE-CHECKED ONLY by every gate list in this repo. The Engine category builds RenderTest but has no `test RenderTest` line, and no category declares `Games/RenderTest/**` in its `paths`, so the union cannot add one. Do not treat such a test as evidence unless you ran it by hand and say so.","bp9jeufcanmqiblw7pq8ax8q":"c-dev-zenith","dm4mxfvxv5eug34ch759t5ra":"ZEN-12","hns5iycp45kq5mllb4zat8zx":"NOTHING locks it. There is no gate line that runs any RenderTest automated test, which is the finding. `Tools/unit_baselines.json` additionally declares the RenderTest row `advisory` -- nothing runs `run_unit_gate.ps1 -Game RenderTest` either -- so RenderTest is the game with the least mechanical coverage despite being compiled by every Engine tick.","m60k4ui1qewy9tu9u5u1edvb":"ZEN-12's Definition of Done required a headless proof that two views with different destinations produce identical pass lists. ~115 lines implementing it landed in `Test_RenderGraphViewStructure.cpp` and every gate went green without executing a line of it. The RenderTest boot count moving 2800->2801 looks like confirmation and is not: that +1 is a `ZENITH_TEST` boot unit in `Flux_RenderViews.Tests.inl`, while `RT_RenderGraphViewStructure` is a harness test the unit gate never reaches. Surfaced by the ZEN-12 reviewer, not by any gate. Run it with `rendertest.exe --automated-test RT_RenderGraphViewStructure --skip-unit-tests` -- it is backend-neutral and `requiresGraphics` is false, so the Null exe the gate already built will run it. Done for ZEN-12: 2217 checks, 0 failed, clause 5b reporting `slot 5 declared 43 passes, slot 6 declared 43`. This is the same blast-radius family as the rule that the Engine gate list must name every game: building a game proves its tests COMPILE, never that they RAN.","vl51anabw4bazm7tvt72na7h":"easy","zjr55or91hidtu1kp33iu7vx":"Testing","zp5jckpmecaw3p49w2bbzzfh":"2026-09-19"},"created_at":"2026-09-19T21:48:37.577Z","updated_at":"2026-09-19T21:48:37.577Z"},{"id":"4ff2f908-1254-4f35-b804-b6e4daa2f241","database_id":"gm1dzh0b1o8u1p38sosvoco4","values":{"bih0nae73jl5qkv6uih6task":"ZEN-D-004","bjs5nsf3nkc4eea6d4kvfrli":"ANY `--automated-test` boot authors scenes, on EITHER backend -- not just a windowed one. Check `git status` after every automated-test run and restore drift that is not the ticket's work, before staging anything.","bp9jeufcanmqiblw7pq8ax8q":"c-dev-zenith","dm4mxfvxv5eug34ch759t5ra":"ZEN-12","hns5iycp45kq5mllb4zat8zx":"Nothing automated. `zagent guard` sees the files only if they are still dirty at guard time, and the excursion check only reports files that reach the commit -- neither distinguishes ticket work from capture drift. The discipline is the check.","m60k4ui1qewy9tu9u5u1edvb":"Measured repeatedly during ZEN-12. Windowed `Vulkan_*_True` boots of DevilsPlayground and Zenithmon each re-authored a committed `.zscen` (`ProcLevel.zscen`, `Dawnmere.zscen`) and created an untracked `Games/Zenithmon/Assets/Authored/Creatures/Fernfawn/`, on a clean tree, BOTH before and after the source change -- so it is drift from the shipped binaries, not from any diff. A `Null_` HEADLESS boot of `rendertest.exe --automated-test RT_RenderGraphViewStructure` then dirtied `Games/RenderTest/Assets/Scenes/RenderTest.zscen` the same way. That last one matters because the protocol's warning is phrased as `a WINDOWED test run is authoring`: ZEN-6 removed the headless `.zscen` publish guard, so headless boots author too and the warning's scope is stale. Left unrestored, a `git add -A` at commit time sweeps unrelated committed scenes into the ticket. Separately worth noting: Zenithmon's own CLAUDE.md states a boot must NOT leave a scene modified in `git status`, so that invariant is currently broken on master independently of any ticket.","vl51anabw4bazm7tvt72na7h":"easy","zjr55or91hidtu1kp33iu7vx":"engine","zp5jckpmecaw3p49w2bbzzfh":"2026-09-19"},"created_at":"2026-09-19T21:48:43.147Z","updated_at":"2026-09-19T21:48:43.147Z"},{"id":"b484dbdb-3adc-4045-874d-df4b378d4b48","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-005","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"A frame-local render queue that is gated on a display option must be consumed UNCONDITIONALLY every frame. Gating the DRAIN on the option is an unbounded-accumulation bug.\n\nFlux has three debug/overlay channels and before ZEN-40 they handled this three different ways. `Flux_Text` is correct and says so in a comment on `ExecuteRenderGraphPass`: it calls `DiscardPendingFrame()` on the disabled path, \"so consume the complete frame boundary instead of replaying stale text when the option is re-enabled\". `Flux_Quads` is correct by a different route: it gates SUBMISSION on the option, so nothing is ever queued. `Flux_Primitives` did neither -- `ExecuteGBuffer` drained and Clear()'d its six debug instance queues only inside `if (bDebugPrimitivesEnabled)`, and its early return ANDed the same flag into `bHaveDebugPrimitives`, so a disabled non-empty queue returned without clearing at all.\n\nWHY, measured on ZEN-40: a photo tour disables `m_bPrimitivesEnabled` for its whole duration (Games/RenderTest/Tests/PhotoTour.cpp:353-354, restored at :572), so the queues grew for the length of the tour and the entire backlog was recorded in ONE frame when Teardown restored the option. `EmitPrimitiveDraw` issues one `BindDrawConstants` per instance at 80 bytes, rounded up to the device's minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment (128 on the reporting machine), against a 131072-byte per-worker Vulkan scratch partition -- an overflow at 1024 draws, reported as `Worker 1 scratch buffer overflow (offset=262144, size=128, end=262144)` with a 0x80000003 exit.\n\nThe generalisation for any future Flux channel: the option controls what is DRAWN, never whether the backlog is RETIRED.\n\nCorollary worth keeping: the Vulkan scratch allocator (`Zenith_Vulkan_PerFrame::AllocateScratchBuffer`) is a pure bump allocator reset only in `BeginFrame()`. It is therefore the DETECTOR of this class of bug, not the defect. Raising `uSCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE` only moves the number in the assert, which Docs/design/Photorealism.md had already observed (1 MB -> 4 MB -> 16 MB) without identifying the producer.\n","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T10:50:53.374Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T10:50:53.374Z"},{"id":"56b6141f-54f6-4d8a-8926-1c7bd24207d8","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-006","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"`Tools/doc_lint.ps1` Check 7 (Check-LivePin) reconciles a game's Status.md LIVE PIN block against Tools/unit_baselines.json -- but NO Engine-category gate ever runs doc_lint, for any game. So the one check written to catch pin-narration drift is unreachable from exactly the tickets most likely to cause it.\n\nMeasured on ZEN-40: Zenithmon's LIVE PIN line read 4551/2698/2801 while unit_baselines.json already held 4556/2703/2806 -- five units of un-narrated drift accumulated since ZEN-12. C7 would have failed on that the moment it ran; its own header comment records the same incident one bump smaller (\"LIVE PIN read 3387 while Tools/unit_baselines.json held 3388\").\n\nWHY it was unreachable: `doc_lint.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` is declared in the Zenithmon category's gate list in zagent.project.json. A ticket only runs it when `zagent gates` unions the Zenithmon category in, which happens when the diff touches Games/Zenithmon/**. The Engine category's own gate list -- eleven game builds, `test Combat`, and the Combat unit gate -- contains no doc_lint line at all.\n\nThe consequence is structural, not incidental: a backend-neutral engine unit moves EVERY game's pinned row (this ticket moved all three), so the tickets that change the most pins are precisely the engine tickets whose gate list cannot check any Status.md narration. ZEN-40 ran C7 only by luck, because its diff happens to touch Games/Zenithmon/Docs/.\n\nRecorded rather than fixed here because zagent.project.json is a protectedPath; the fix is a human edit adding a doc_lint line (or lines) to the Engine gate list, and it should be weighed against the cost of running doc_lint for every game on every engine ticket.\n\nFound by the ZEN-40 review. The first draft of the Status.md narration asserted the opposite -- that doc_lint does not compare these numbers at all -- which was a fabricated mechanism written without opening doc_lint.ps1.\n","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T10:50:59.694Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T10:50:59.694Z"},{"id":"b7a06b53-f6b7-47da-989b-aa998fbce6e6","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-007","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"The Vault write layer validates before it mutates, structurally, and this is the guarantee every zagent refusal rests on.\n\n`executeOperation` (Tools/Vault/server/operations.mjs) calls `options.prepare(index)` at line 321. The journal is written at line 368 and applied/committed at line 369. Therefore no byte of the vault work tree and no git commit can exist before `prepare` returns a change set. A command handler that throws inside its `prepare` callback has, by construction, changed nothing.\n\n`runOperation` (Tools/Vault/cli/write.mjs:538) is the single door every CLI mutation goes through, and it catches thrown `WriteError`s and maps them to exit codes (INVALID->4, OWNERSHIP/STALE/LOCKED->5, EMPTY->3, BREAKER->6). So the rule generalises past `claim` to every write command: put validation inside `prepare`, before the `changes` array is constructed, and atomicity is free.\n\nTwo pre-`prepare` writes exist and are deliberately NOT board state: the operation lock ref `refs/vault/operation-lock` (released in a `finally`) and `.git/vault/authority.json`. `recoverLocked(ctx)` also runs before `prepare` and CAN write and commit -- but only to finish a previous operation's interrupted journal, i.e. bytes some earlier operation already validated. Never the current caller's data.\n\nWHY this is worth recording: the old SQL board did the opposite -- it mutated then validated, which is the defect the 2026-08-24 CRITICAL Suggestions row describes and which ZEN-79 was filed to reproduce against Vault. It does not reproduce. Anyone auditing a future zagent refusal should check the same three lines (321 / 368 / 369) rather than re-deriving the argument, and anyone ADDING a write command should know that validation placed after the change set is built would silently reintroduce the old defect.\n\nPinned by Tools/Vault/test/claim-refusal-atomicity.test.mjs, whose fixture sets `writes.commit = true` (unlike the other self-built CLI fixtures, which disable commits and would make a \"no commit\" assertion trivially true) and which includes a control test around an ACCEPTED claim so the refusal probes cannot pass vacuously.\n","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T10:51:05.733Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T10:51:05.733Z"},{"id":"ef325e6b-7b92-4d48-a3dc-120d133f0f52","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-008","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"Board state imported by the Vault activation snapshot is NOT evidence about Vault's behaviour, and at least one anomaly has already been misattributed that way.\n\nCommit 3f7b3a59 \"Activate Vault from the frozen production board snapshot\" (2026-09-16) imported the old SQL board's rows wholesale, including each ticket's then-current `status` and `assignee`. Eleven ZEN tickets arrived already carrying an agent assignee. Commit 688273cc then renamed the retired identity `agent@saas.invalid` -> `agent@zenith.invalid` across board data, so those rows afterwards read as assigned to the CURRENT agent.\n\nThat is the whole origin of the \"eight ZEN tickets assigned to the agent while still To Do\" observed on 2026-09-19 (ZEN-3, ZEN-12, ZEN-14, ZEN-16, ZEN-18, ZEN-19, ZEN-20, ZEN-22 -- the eleven minus three that had since reached Done). They were cleared by eight `board: update` commits the same day. No Vault `claim` ever ran on them in that state.\n\nWHY it matters: ZEN-79 was filed on the reasoning that those eight \"are the same shape\" as the SQL board's mutate-before-validate defect and therefore suggested the defect had survived the port. They ARE the same shape -- because they are literally the residue of that defect, frozen into the snapshot -- but they say nothing about the new implementation, which validates before it mutates (see the companion decision on Vault write ordering).\n\nThe generalisable rule: before treating a board-data anomaly as evidence of a live CLI defect, check whether the rows predate 3f7b3a59. `git log --format=\"COMMIT %h %ad %s\" --date=short -p -- Zenith/Docs/Board/tickets/<KEY>.md` answers it in one command, and a `+status:` / `+assignee:` pair appearing in that activation commit means the state was inherited, not produced.\n","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T10:51:11.861Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T10:51:11.861Z"},{"id":"320c05a2-63aa-46ea-bb99-2a22889968c6","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-009","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"In PowerShell, `Get-Content` on a SINGLE-LINE file returns a String, not an array -- so `$lines = Get-Content $f; for ($i=0; $i -lt $lines.Length; $i++) { $line = $lines[$i] }` iterates CHARACTERS and the loop body silently never sees a line. Always write `$lines = @(Get-Content $f)`.\n\nMeasured on pwsh 7 during ZEN-8:\n\n    one.md  -> type=String    .Length=24  $lines[0]='S'\n    many.md -> type=Object[]  .Length=3   $lines[0]='line one'\n\nWHY it is worth a decision rather than a code comment: the failure is SILENT and DATA-DEPENDENT. A line-oriented linter written this way works perfectly on every real document in the repo, because living docs are always multi-line, and reports nothing at all on a one-line file. ZEN-8's new C9 check shipped with this bug; it was caught only because the ticket required a test that fails without the check, and the test's fixtures happened to be single-line. Six of that test's ten assertions were also passing VACUOUSLY for the same reason -- they asserted \"no violation appears\", which is equally true when the check is broken.\n\nTHIS IS NOT FIXED REPO-WIDE. `Tools/doc_lint.ps1` has EIGHT `$lines = Get-Content` sites and ZEN-8 wrapped only its own (the C9 read site). Lines 152, 262, 282, 315, 349, 434 and 519 -- i.e. every other line-oriented check, C1 through C8 -- still carry it. They are latent, not dormant by design: point any of those checks at a one-line doc and it passes without looking.\n\nThe generalisation, which is the part worth carrying: **a test whose only assertion is that nothing was reported cannot distinguish \"the rule holds\" from \"the checker never ran\".** Pair every such assertion with a positive control in the same input -- something that MUST be reported -- so the test fails both when the rule breaks and when detection goes silent. ZEN-8's suppression assertions were rewritten that way, and the same reasoning independently produced the accepted-claim control test in ZEN-79's atomicity suite (see ZEN-D-007). Two tickets in one session needed it; it is a general property of proof-of-absence tests, not a quirk of either.\n","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T10:51:17.954Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T10:51:17.954Z"},{"id":"ef19d48a-3a9f-4125-9eed-6a9f2ae6a5ae","database_id":"v98et4f3ozbmfonxuavdrrrq","values":{"rlwt4zm5xtrwqk2t2hbwolsx":"Tools/Vault","qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"The Vault vitest suite has parallel-execution flakiness: three full runs on 2026-09-20 each produced exactly one failure, in a DIFFERENT file each time (test/issue-interactions.test.mjs > comment deletion uses strict CAS...; test/issue-ui.test.jsx > IssuePanel loads detail...; test/write-branches.test.mjs > sprint lifecycle covers create, start...). Every one passed in isolation on re-run (11/11, 17/17, 18/18). All three touch the write/interaction path, which suggests shared temp-fixture or operation-lock contention under vitest's default parallelism rather than three independent bugs. Impact: `npm test` cannot be used as a gate line verdict without a re-run policy, and the new Tooling gate category runs it. Suggested next step: run with --pool=forks or --poolOptions.threads.singleThread and see whether the flakiness disappears, which would localise it to shared state rather than timing.","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"medium","h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"open","fgvpu8fja84411t89jvzgvs0":"ZEN-14","kutn19z061622yllp5eqj5ah":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T11:22:23.191Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T11:22:23.191Z"},{"id":"34da2781-ed59-4740-9860-721d1be717ab","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-010","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"`zagent.project.json` is the authority for gates and categories, and the Vault reads it FRESH on every call. It stopped doing so at the cutover, and the failure was silent for four days.\n\n`vault.config.json` embeds a SNAPSHOT of the file, taken by the migration, with no sync step. Worse, it embeds it TWICE: `policy.client.file` (what `policyOf` reads) and `policy.resolved.projects.<KEY>.categories` (what `gatesOf` and `gateSelectionOf` read). Fixing only the first makes a config edit APPEAR to work -- `policyOf` reports the new categories -- while the gate list a tick actually runs stays stale.\n\nMEASURED 2026-09-20: the on-disk file declared 15 Engine gate lines and a `Tooling` category; `zagent gates ZEN-14` resolved 13 and no `Tooling`. Two gate-coverage fixes committed that same morning (`fa8ad5b2`) were therefore inert -- including the `Tooling` category whose entire purpose was to close \"no gate runs non-C++ code\", and the `doc_lint` lines closing ZEN-D-006.\n\nWHY IT WAS SILENT, and the part worth carrying: **a gate list that is merely SHORTER still goes green.** There is no signal for \"the gates you thought you configured did not run\". Every existing control checks whether the gates that DID run passed. This is the same shape as the union defect the `paths` mechanism was built for, one level further up: there, a category's gates were missing from a ticket; here, the category itself was missing from the config the selector read.\n\nRoot CLAUDE.md had already stated both the rule and the reason, before the backend that broke it existed: *\"The file is sent every time rather than registered once. A stored copy goes stale, and a stale gate list is exactly how a green run ratchets the wrong pinned baseline.\"*\n\nThe generalisation: **when a migration embeds a copy of a file that a human is documented to edit, the copy wins silently and the document becomes a lie.** Prefer reading the authority; if a snapshot is unavoidable, make the staleness loud (compare and refuse) rather than letting the reader pick. And when you find one embedded copy, GREP FOR A SECOND -- here there were two, in the same file, and the second is the one that mattered.\n\nFixed in `eee6a419`; pinned by `Tools/Vault/test/project-file-authority.test.mjs` (8 tests, 5 of which fail if the overlay is reverted).\n","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T11:22:53.004Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T11:22:53.004Z"},{"id":"b9b7977c-1853-46f0-897c-95387cf26677","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Give `Build/**` a home in `zagent.project.json` categories — either add it to `Engine.paths` or give the build system its own category — so a Sharpmake-only diff unions in the engine gate list instead of zero gates.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Measured 2026-09-20 via effectiveGates: a diff touching only `Build/Sharpmake_Zenith.cs` filed under a non-Engine category resolves 5 gate lines and unions in NOTHING, while `Zenith/ZenithECS/Zenith_Scene.h` resolves 18 (Engine) and `Tools/doc_lint.ps1` resolves 16 (Tooling). `Build/**` is the file set that decides what every game compiles and which TUs land in which lib — Sharpmake_Zenith.cs alone carries the 10 build-exclude regexes that partition the leaf libs from the aggregate — and a wrong edit there is a duplicate-symbol link break or a silently dropped TU in every game. It is currently the least covered important directory in the repo. Same family as ZEN-D-010: nothing reports a gate list that is merely shorter.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed by the first option the row offered: Build/** joins the Engine category paths in zagent.project.json, with a comment recording why it belongs to Engine rather than Tooling -- the blast radius is every game compile, which the Engine list already exists to cover, not a Tooling-shaped npm test or lint script. MEASURED against the real selector before and after: a diff touching only Build/Sharpmake_Zenith.cs went from 5 gate lines with nothing unioned in, to the full Engine-unioned list matching what a Zenith/ZenithECS/Zenith_Scene.h diff resolves. Confirmed Build/** did not swallow Tools/**: a cli/client.mjs-only diff still unions Tooling alone."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T11:38:18.063Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T11:38:18.063Z"},{"id":"853f3df8-b0ba-49ed-8e03-ffda2a0ba0e0","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"Moving engine source OUT of `Zenith/` also moves it out of the Engine gate category, so any such move needs a `zagent.project.json` edit LANDED FIRST — by a human, because the guard refuses that file.\n\n`Engine.paths` is exactly `[\"Zenith/**\"]`, and the aggregate engine glob is `SourceRootPath = RootPath + \"/Zenith\"` (recursive). Those two facts make \"outside the aggregate glob\" and \"inside the Engine gate category\" mutually exclusive: the directory predicate that a Sharpmake partition wants and the directory predicate that gate selection uses are the same string, serving opposite purposes.\n\nMeasured on ZEN-14 (2026-09-20): a diff touching `Libs/ZenithECS/**` resolves 5 gate lines and unions in nothing, against 18 for the same file at `Zenith/ZenithECS/**`. The move would have removed 13 of 18 gate lines from every future change to the engine's ECS, Physics and AI leaves, with every gate green — the ZEN-D-010 shape, where a merely shorter gate list is reported by nothing.\n\nConsequences: (1) a ticket proposing to relocate engine source is not loop-completable as filed, however unprotected its own file list looks — the reachability scan reads the DoD for NAMED protected paths and cannot infer one from a directory move; (2) the prerequisite is safe to land early, since adding a not-yet-existing root to `Engine.paths` matches nothing and changes no current selection; (3) the same trap applies to `Tools/complexity_profiles.json`, whose `singleton_ratchet` glob and lints `scope_globs` are also keyed on `Zenith/**` — those ARE loop-editable and must move in the same commit.\n\nGeneral form: when a path glob is load-bearing for two different systems — here a build partition and a gate selector — moving a directory satisfies one and silently breaks the other, and only the build one fails loudly.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"uncategorized"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T11:38:46.162Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T11:38:46.162Z"},{"id":"10c3c824-29e2-45d1-949a-18d64e56056b","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"A `git mv` under `Zenith/**` can break an allowlist that lives in `Tools/Vault/test/*.mjs`, and NO gate list that covers `Zenith/**` runs the suite that would catch it.\n\nMeasured on ZEN-101. `Tools/Vault/test/saas-guard.test.mjs` carries a deliberately narrow path allowlist for the one known false positive of the retired-name guard (`MSAASamples`, a Vulkan multisampling field whose lowercase form contains the hunted string). It read `['Middleware/', 'Zenith/Vulkan/']`. Commit `12eb38b8` renamed `Zenith/Vulkan/` to `Zenith/RenderBackends/Vulkan/`, which silently broke that prefix and left the guard RED from that commit onward.\n\nTwo independent reasons nothing caught it:\n\n1. The refactor's own re-path inventory searched `Tools/**` for `.ps1`/`.psm1` and reported no hits. The allowlist is in a `.mjs` TEST file, so the extension filter walked past it.\n2. `Tools/Vault/**` belongs to the `Tooling` category; `Zenith/**` belongs to `Engine`. The gate union only ADDS the categories a diff actually touches, so an engine-wide directory move never runs the Vault suite. It surfaced on ZEN-101 only because an unrelated excursion into `Tools/tick_gates.ps1` pulled `Tooling` into the union.\n\nThe general rule: **when re-pathing after a directory move, grep every tracked file type, not the ones the code is written in.** Allowlists, fixtures and guards live in whatever language their harness uses.
