And a category mapping cannot express \"this directory's contents are named in another category's test data\" — the union is a lower bound on blast radius, not an upper one.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"uncategorized"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T20:10:40.028Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T20:10:40.029Z"},{"id":"d12a316f-d2dc-49ae-a9f4-ffdfd2964d08","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-011","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"`@(SomeFunction)` RE-WRAPS a `return , $arr` in PowerShell — and `Tools/tick_gates.ps1` had exactly one such call site, which crashed `-Phase measure` for every ticket that created no `.inl`.\n\n`Get-CreatedIncludeFiles` ends `return , $created.ToArray()`. The leading comma is the idiom that carries an EMPTY array through the pipeline intact: the function emits ONE object (the array). Collecting that in `@(...)` therefore produces an array of one element whose `[0]` is the inner array — so `.Count` was always 1, the guarding `if ($newIncludes.Count -gt 0)` was always true, the loop always ran, and with no created `.inl` the single element was `@()`. `Split-Path -Leaf @()` throws \"Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is an empty array\", and `-Phase measure` exits 1 AFTER every build has already passed.\n\nThree things worth keeping:\n\n1. **The correct pattern was 60 lines above it.** `$created = Get-CreatedSourceFiles` — plain assignment — consumes the sibling function correctly. Plain assignment captures the single emitted object, which IS the array. Never wrap a `return , $arr` call in `@()`.\n2. **This check sits OUTSIDE the `if ($newFiles.Count -gt 0)` block**, so whether a source file was created is irrelevant — it threw on every measure run with no created `.inl`, which is an entirely ordinary ticket shape.\n3. **`Tools/Test_TickGates.ps1` passes both before and after the fix.** The harness's own test suite does not cover the zero-created-`.inl` path, so the only thing that detected this was running it on a real ticket.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-101","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"uncategorized"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T20:11:45.322Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T20:11:45.322Z"},{"id":"ddaf3aff-6695-45bc-bdd0-0ce444d57a4c","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-012","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"A `git mv` under `Zenith/**` can break an allowlist that lives in `Tools/Vault/test/*.mjs`, and NO gate list that covers `Zenith/**` runs the suite that would catch it.\n\nMeasured on ZEN-101. `Tools/Vault/test/saas-guard.test.mjs` carries a deliberately narrow path allowlist for the one known false positive of the retired-name guard (`MSAASamples`, a Vulkan multisampling field whose lowercase form contains the hunted string). It read `['Middleware/', 'Zenith/Vulkan/']`. Commit `12eb38b8` renamed `Zenith/Vulkan/` to `Zenith/RenderBackends/Vulkan/`, which silently broke that prefix and left the guard RED from that commit onward.\n\nTwo independent reasons nothing caught it:\n\n1. The refactor's own re-path inventory searched `Tools/**` for `.ps1`/`.psm1` and reported no hits. The allowlist is in a `.mjs` TEST file, so the extension filter walked past it.\n2. `Tools/Vault/**` belongs to the `Tooling` category; `Zenith/**` belongs to `Engine`. The gate union only ADDS the categories a diff actually touches, so an engine-wide directory move never runs the Vault suite. It surfaced on ZEN-101 only because an unrelated excursion into `Tools/tick_gates.ps1` pulled `Tooling` into the union.\n\nThe general rule: **when re-pathing after a directory move, grep every tracked file type, not the ones the code is written in.** Allowlists, fixtures and guards live in whatever language their harness uses. And a category mapping cannot express \"this directory's contents are named in another category's test data\" — the union is a lower bound on blast radius, not an upper one.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-101","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"uncategorized"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T20:12:04.759Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T20:12:04.759Z"},{"id":"ff7e41a5-b520-403b-ba9a-7f53ed3fa087","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Three tick-harness defects found while running ZEN-101. One is fixed in that commit; these three are NOT, and each is reported rather than patched because none blocked the ticket once worked around.\n\n**1. `-Phase measure` is NOT IDEMPOTENT — the by-name build-log assertion false-positives on an incremental build.**\n`tick_gates.ps1` proves a created `.cpp` reached the compiler by grepping the build log for its basename. On a COLD build the name appears and the check passes; on an INCREMENTAL build where nothing recompiled, no TU is named at all and the check reports `NOT IN BUILD LOG` and exits 3 — \"the build is green and the deliverable is not in it\". Measured on ZEN-101: measure run 1 printed `compiled: Zenith_AssetRegistryPCH.cpp`, run 2 (nothing changed but a `.ps1` comment) printed `NOT IN BUILD LOG` for the same file. Direct evidence contradicted it — the `.obj` was on disk and the `.lib` contained all 13 objects.\nThis matters because the protocol MANDATES re-running a phase after any post-measure edit, so hitting it is normal, not a corner case. It fails CLOSED, which is the safe direction, but it costs a full build cycle and reads as a deliverable defect when it is not. The workaround is `zenith clean engine` before re-measuring.\nSuggested fix: assert the `.obj` exists under the project's `IntermediatePath` rather than grepping the build log. Strictly stronger AND idempotent.\n\n**2. A crashed phase reports `state: complete`, all steps green, and `skipped: []` while gate lines never ran.**\nMeasure run 1 crashed in a post-build assertion. The resulting `tick_gates.json` read `state: complete`, 12 steps all `exitCode: 0`, `skipped: []` — while `test Combat`, the unit gate and both `doc_lint` lines had never executed and were not listed anywhere. The only tell was the top-level `exitCode: 1`, which is not a value in the documented ladder (0/2/3/4/5/10).\n`zagent guard`'s freshness fold checks `state` and `headSha` only, both of which were fine, so it would not override a would-be pass on this shape. The protocol tells the reader to trust the JSON over the shell and to read `skipped` — and here the JSON's own `skipped` was empty and wrong.\nSuggested fix: on any internal-error exit path, populate `skipped` with every gate line that never ran, and have `guard` treat a non-zero `exitCode` in the verdict the same way it treats a stale `headSha`.\n\n**3. `zagent decide` mints no ID unless `--ticket`/`--project` is passed — and `zagent finish` requires one.**\n`zagent decide --file x.md` records the row with `ID: null`. `zagent finish` refuses any terminal status whose work log does not carry `**Durable findings**: none` or refs shaped `PROJ-D-N`. So filing a decision the natural way produces a row that cannot be cited by the work log of the very tick that filed it. Measured on ZEN-101: the same file re-filed with `--project ZEN --ticket ZEN-101` minted `ZEN-D-012`. At least five existing rows in the decisions DB carry `ID: null` for what is presumably the same reason, and the DB is append-only so the un-IDed rows cannot be tidied.\nSuggested fix: default `--ticket` to the in-flight claim, or refuse a `decide` that cannot mint an ID, rather than silently recording an uncitable row.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"(not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"All three addressed. (1) The by-name build-log grep is replaced by an .obj presence check as the authority -- for a game file the exact Games/<Name>/Build/obj/win64/<config> path, for a shared engine file a search across every lib obj tree, deliberately NOT a second copy of the 32-lib Sharpmake membership table. Strictly stronger and idempotent, so the mandated re-run after a post-measure edit no longer false-fails; the log grep stays as an informational secondary note. (2) PlannedLines and DeferredLines now populate immediately after gate-list classification, before regen or any line runs, so skipped is correct from any exit path including an early crash; the internal-error catch now writes state error rather than complete, which trips guard existing state check for the first time. (3) decide minting an ID without --ticket/--project was already fixed before triage (write.mjs mintDecisionId, covered by decide-reference.test.mjs) -- the row predates that."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T20:12:32.212Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T20:12:32.212Z"},{"id":"963aa60d-4678-43b9-a73e-76ff6b43870d","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-013","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"Removing glm from the `Zenith.h` precompiled header trades ONE parse per PCH for ONE parse per consuming translation unit — and on this codebase that is ~600-1000+ TUs against 13 PCHs, so it is very likely a large net BUILD-TIME REGRESSION, not the improvement the idea is usually filed as.\n\nMeasured on master, 2026-09-20 (ZEN-100):\n\n- `Zenith.h` -> `Maths/Zenith_Maths.h` -> 4 glm includes, whose resolved closure is **202 glm headers** (203 total). That figure is exact.\n- `glm/fwd.hpp`'s closure is **5 headers**. So the PCH-size prize is real and large.\n- But `glm/glm.hpp` ALONE pulls **152 of the 202**, so there is no cheap subset to drop: trimming the three `gtx`/`gtc` includes gets 202 -> 152 and no further, and `glm::quat` (aliased as `Zenith_Maths::Quat`) keeps `gtc/quaternion` mandatory anyway.\n- `Zenith_Maths::Vector3` and friends are `using` ALIASES of glm types (`using Vector3 = glm::vec3;`), so anything holding one BY VALUE — a struct member, a by-value parameter, a return — needs the complete type. Forward declaration only helps declaration-only consumers.\n- **587 of 1593 `.cpp` (37%) reference `Zenith_Maths::` or `glm::` directly. So do 261 `.h` and 176 `.inl`.** Those 261 headers are the multiplier: a header with a `Vector3` member must include the heavy maths header itself, so every TU including it re-parses the 202 headers. The reach is therefore far larger than the 587 direct TUs.\n\nToday glm is parsed **13 times** (once per PCH-creating library, per the >=4-TU rule). After the change it would be parsed once per consuming TU. The PCH shrinks — each is currently 119 MB (Debug_True) to 192 MB (Release_True) — and `Build/obj` shrinks with it, but compile time for the ~40-60% of TUs that need glm gets worse, not better.\n\n**The ruling nobody has made is whether that disk-for-time trade is wanted**, and a DoD phrased as \"a representative `Zenith.pch` is measurably smaller\" would be satisfied by a change that makes every build slower. That is the shape where green gates answer a narrower question than they appear to.\n\nWhat a correctly-scoped version looks like: prototype the flip, measure cold AND incremental build time before/after on a fixed config, and accept or reject on that number rather than on PCH size. `Zenith_MathsFwd.h` is cheap to build and worth having regardless — the expensive, irreversible half is repointing `Zenith.h` at it.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-100","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"uncategorized"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T20:23:51.668Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T20:23:51.668Z"},{"id":"7af4d3ed-0340-4277-91e0-0f4c3d035765","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-014","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"Flux_GraphicsImpl::UploadRenderViewConstants is NOT a pre-gather seam and must never be used as one: it runs INSIDE render-graph Execute, after the Prepare/gather callbacks.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Its sole caller is Flux.cpp:109 inside Flux_RendererImpl::RecordFrame, whose sole caller is Flux/RenderGraph/Flux_RenderGraph_Execution.cpp:147 -- i.e. inside graph Execute, and Flux.cpp:98-99 states in as many words that CallPrepareCallbacks ran before it. Anything that must be ready BEFORE the unified mesh cull's Prepare (cascade view-proj matrices, above all) cannot be staged there. ZEN-19's ticket body suggested exactly this as an alternative home for UpdateShadowMatrices; acting on that suggestion would move the cascade matrices to after the cull Prepare and reintroduce the last-frame-frusta bug Flux/Shadows/CLAUDE.md records as the reason for the existing hoist. The name reads like a pre-frame step and the file's own header comment says 'Main thread, once per frame, before the persistent VIEW sets are written', which is true and misleading -- 'before the VIEW sets' is inside Execute, not before it.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"hard","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-19","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T21:36:00.473Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T21:36:00.473Z"},{"id":"431544b2-9ca9-4a2e-9445-2afa47a1fdd0","database_id":"ei3xsxd2a5zto5fqkxkfddor","values":{"osj2s7mvgu3b10m6i5mt1m2f":"2026-09-20","hwrf69f9qt2hykb4vlibjxvd":"ZEN-19: should Flux_FeatureRegistry grow an optional fifth per-frame trampoline (a main-thread pre-gather hook) so Flux_ShadowsImpl DECLARES its cascade-matrix update the way it already declares Initialise/SetupRenderGraph/Shutdown/BuildPipelines -- or is the landed forwarder the intended end state?","mnn9e0j18lj2gt7t7uhdrq4w":"medium","j5tx2uhkidipafnfaiwjq370":"open","e19vi1mcn25elwvwabvzoxa8":"ZEN-19","xe6176yhgtsnstwiz9t8e4ex":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T21:36:23.487Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T21:36:23.487Z"},{"id":"5024d076-336a-4826-af84-372cb5302e57","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-015","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-20","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"In Tools/Vault/cli/write.mjs's appendKnowledgeRow, the project used for ROUTING and for the catalog-less refusal must stay narrow; only the project used to MINT a PROJ-D-N id may carry the checkout-default fallback chain. They are two variables now (project / mintProject) and must not be recombined.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"ZEN-99 asked for the single `project` derivation to be widened to match the four siblings at write.mjs:594/844/1006/1103. That was implemented first and is a MEASURED REGRESSION, caught by zagent-reviewer and confirmed by running the suite: `project` feeds three consumers, not one -- knowledgeRecord (WHERE the row goes), the `!project` guard at ~:1380 (whether that is answerable at all), and mintDecisionId (what the id is called). Widening it makes the guard pass in a vault with no catalog, so a bare `zagent ask` with no --ticket and no --project stops refusing with exit 1/CONFIGURATION and instead silently creates <PROJECT>/knowledge/questions.md and returns 0. Tools/Vault/test/write-branches.test.mjs ('knowledge falls back to the metadata catalog and to a new knowledge file', assertions at ~:673-675) is the coverage that caught it. General form: a variable whose name describes a NOUN ('project') but which is consumed by decisions of different consequence -- one cosmetic (what to call a thing), one structural (whether to write at all) -- cannot be widened for the cosmetic consumer without loosening the structural one. Split it before widening it.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-99","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"Tooling"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:24:55.013Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:24:55.013Z"},{"id":"8b505801-fc55-4d79-8e17-396d9537ea18","database_id":"v98et4f3ozbmfonxuavdrrrq","values":{"qk1c8p6tcrgrmn4gp0dq2s89":"The Tools/Vault Vitest suite has at least TWO distinct intermittent failures on Windows, and either one reds the whole Tooling gate list -- which stops the five doc_lint lines behind it from running at all.","jys5sx59va7xc7796hit60mr":"high","h0plfp8fp5xkfizdcomb5mol":"open","fgvpu8fja84411t89jvzgvs0":"ZEN-99"},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:25:19.209Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:25:19.209Z"},{"id":"ecd55eea-3fc4-4cf1-a8c7-84bb8d7612f8","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"`tick_gates.ps1 -Phase measure` reports a GREEN verdict in tick_gates.json having run ZERO gate lines, whenever the category has no unit-gate line.\n\nMeasured on ZEN-99 (category Tooling, 12 gate lines): the JSON came back `{state: complete, exitCode: 0, steps: [], skipped: []}`. The console log is honest — it prints `NO unit-gate line in this gate list -- no pin was measured`, lists all 12 lines as `deferred:`, and then prints `all gates green (exit 0)`. The JSON carries none of that.\n\ntick.md designates tick_gates.json as THE trustworthy channel (\"READ .zagent/run/<KEY>/tick_gates.json. Full stop — not 'the exit code, or the JSON'\") precisely because the shell exit code and the harness notification are corruptible. So the one channel the protocol says to trust is the one that omits the deferral, while the channel it says not to trust is the one that reports it.\n\nSuggest the measure phase either write the deferred lines into a `deferred` array alongside `skipped`, or refuse to report exitCode 0 when `steps` is empty.\n\nThis is a sharper instance of open ticket ZEN-78: ZEN-78 is about reporting deferrals, this is about the VERDICT itself being indistinguishable from a full green run.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"An orchestrator following tick.md literally — read the JSON, branch on it — sees a green verdict for a phase that executed nothing. In this tick it was caught only because the Tooling gate list was short enough to notice that 12 lines had not run. On a longer list, or unattended under /loop, a measure-phase verdict that verified nothing reads identically to one that verified everything.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"blocks-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-99","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed the stronger way the row offered: Write-Result in Tools/tick_gates.ps1 now REFUSES to report exitCode 0 when steps is empty, rewriting the verdict to a new code 8 whose string contains \"no gate lines\". Scoped to the 0 case only, so a legitimately red zero-step result is untouched. Code 8 rather than the first free number: 6 is free in this script own ladder but already means circuit-breaker-open in the zagent ladder, and a tick reads both, often in the same step -- the header now documents that reasoning so nobody reclaims 6. An assertion pins the value 8 and explicitly asserts it is not 6. The consumer side matches: cli/tick-checks.mjs added 8 to its documented-ladder set but treats it as NOT fresh with its own reason, since 8 is the one documented code that carries no evidence -- 2/3/4/5 are real current answers about the tree, 8 means nothing was verified. A guard passing on an 8 was exactly this defect."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:30:34.646Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:30:34.646Z"},{"id":"d5c057fc-5805-47ef-bda0-eb649ec01aae","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"`zagent update <KEY> --label blocked-scope` is refused when tick_gates.json shows a genuine RED (exit 2/3/4). That rule is correct for a deterministic red, but it makes the label unreachable in the case where it is most needed: a ticket whose gate list contains a FLAKY suite.\n\nThe Tools/Vault Vitest suite has at least two distinct intermittent failures on Windows (see the ZEN-99 shortfalls row), so a Tooling ticket has a substantial chance of a red it did not cause. tick.md says plainly: \"If the gates went red, it is a failure block whatever else is also true of it.\" Such a ticket therefore becomes a FAILURE block, counts toward maxConsecutiveBlocked, and three of them trip a circuit breaker whose message says the loop is thrashing — when nothing was wrong with any of the three tickets.\n\nSuggest the check consult whether the red SURVIVED the protocol's own flake re-run (red-to-green on the same tree already has a defined meaning in step 7), rather than the raw verdict — or that a recorded flake become a third state alongside green and red.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"ZEN-99's verify #1 came back exit 4 on a flake that vanished on an immediate re-run of the identical command on the identical tree. Had the work ALSO been genuinely out of scope, the honest label would have been refused and the ticket recorded as a failure block on evidence that evaporated one run later.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-99","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed the way the row proposed: the check now consults whether the red SURVIVED a re-run rather than the raw verdict. Producer, Tools/tick_gates.ps1: a red NON-BUILD gate line is re-run once on the same tree and the outcome appended to a new top-level flakes array, each entry line/firstExit/rerunExit. Build lines are excluded because re-running one costs minutes and a build failure is not this flake class. The overall verdict deliberately does NOT change -- a red line stays red and the phase still exits red; flakes is evidence only. Consumer, cli/tick-checks.mjs blockedScopeAllowed: allows the label when every red line is accounted for with a green re-run, refuses and NAMES the surviving line otherwise, and treats a verdict with no flakes key (an older recording) as no evidence, preserving previous behaviour."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:30:52.003Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:30:52.003Z"},{"id":"e6ff134b-2209-4f37-8e10-c1119ec47967","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"contract","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"`zagent contract --json` is documented in TWO committed places and is not implemented. It returns `{\"error\":\"Unknown read command: contract\"}`.\n\nRoot CLAUDE.md gives it its own row in the command table — \"the wire contract as data: the protocol version, which flags are path-valued, which commands ship the docs tree\" — and describes the golden copy living at Tools/zagent/contract.json, \"asserted against by both sides' tests so the path-valued flags and docs-tree commands cannot drift without failing a run on each side\". The tick protocol references it too. The file exists; the command does not.\n\nEither wire the command up to read that file, or delete the two documentation entries. A documented command that errors is worse than an absent one, because it reads as a broken installation rather than a missing feature.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Reached for it during ZEN-99 to enumerate the available commands, after a bare `zagent` and `zagent <cmd> --help` both returned only a usage stub with no command list. Cost a detour into Tools/Vault/cli/client.mjs to read the WRITE_COMMANDS set out of the source instead.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"nuisance","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-99","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Taken the second way the row offered: the documentation was deleted, not the command reinstated. Investigation found contract was removed DELIBERATELY the day before this row was triaged, in commit 4c2bcb17 (the single-local-Vault cutover); Tools/Vault/spec/command-matrix.md records it as removed-transport and declares itself the sole offline specification. Reinstating would have created a second spec alongside it. So the stale half went instead: CLAUDE.md lost the contract table row and the protocol-handshake paragraph (nothing negotiates a version with one local backend), and tick.md lost its reference. The sweep found the same rot elsewhere and removed it too -- the auth mint row (contradicted by the no-token-nothing-to-mint paragraph in the same file), the docs write and docs sync rows (both refuse unconditionally), the Notion mirror section, and exit code 7, which no code path can emit now that there is no network hop. Verified live: no exit-7 emitter, docs status --project genuinely refused, doctor payload exactly as the rewritten row describes. Net -71 lines in CLAUDE.md, -29 in tick.md."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:30:57.703Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:30:57.703Z"},{"id":"a75aba9f-72cb-4457-bd35-d588313720fc","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"`zagent guard <KEY>` on a PASS returns `{ok: true, violations: [], gateSelectionStale: null, docsMirrorNeeded: false, docsMirrorPaths: []}` — with no `gateVerdictFresh` field at all, and `gateSelectionStale` as null rather than false.\n\ntick.md documents the freshness fold as observable on the payload: \"a `state` that isn't `complete`, or a `headSha` that doesn't match current HEAD, turns a would-be PASS into a failure (`gateVerdictFresh: false` on the payload, naming why)\". On a pass there is therefore no positive evidence the fold ran — only the absence of a refusal, which is exactly the shape this protocol distrusts everywhere else. It is the same argument the protocol itself makes for the Coverage row and the Durable-findings line: an explicit answer is visible, a skipped consideration is not.\n\nSuggest emitting `gateVerdictFresh: true` and `gateSelectionStale: false` on the success path, so a passing guard is self-describing.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Observed on both ZEN-19 and ZEN-99. Verified staleness by hand instead — reading headSha out of tick_gates.json and comparing it against `git rev-parse HEAD` — because a clean guard payload could not distinguish 'the fold ran and passed' from 'the fold did not run'.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-19","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed on both halves, so a passing guard is now self-describing. cli/client.mjs stamps gateVerdictFresh true on a genuine exitCode 0 pass, mirroring the existing override branch; cli/local.mjs emits gateSelectionStale false on the clean-with-key path instead of null. The two values stay distinguishable: null still means the fold never ran (no ticket key given), false means it ran and the selection is current, and a message string means stale. Two places had frozen the old buggy value and were updated -- test/cli-entry.test.mjs and the FD-18 case in fixtures/snapshot/reference.json -- with npm run parity confirming 1860/1860 afterwards."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:03.367Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:03.367Z"},{"id":"27c5b04a-5681-48b8-8e5f-d6c705c04864","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"config","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Several open ZEN tickets whose entire deliverable is under Tools/ are filed `category: Engine`, so they resolve the 15-line Engine gate list — eleven game builds plus a Combat test run — for a diff containing zero C++.\n\nMeasured with `zagent show --json`: ZEN-74 (\"zagent claim archives an existing run directory to KEY.prev\"), ZEN-75 (\"zagent writes .zagent/last.exit on every exit path\") and ZEN-98 (\"doc_lint: wrap the seven remaining Get-Content reads\") each report 15 gates. ZEN-99 — the same KIND of work, on the same files — is `category: Tooling` and reports 12, including the assert scripts and the Vault suite that actually EXECUTE such a diff.\n\nThe Tooling category was created for exactly this and is simply not being applied consistently at file time. Suggest re-categorising those three and auditing the rest of the board for the same shape.\n\nNote the gate UNION cannot fix this by itself. It only ADDS the categories a diff touches, so an Engine-categorised Tools/ ticket does get Tooling unioned in — but it still pays for eleven game builds it does not need. The union solves the opposite error (a Tooling ticket that reaches into Zenith/**), not this one.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Not hit directly — ZEN-99 was correctly categorised. Found while surveying candidate tickets for a second tick. The cost is wall-clock: ZEN-19's gate time across measure+verify was dominated by the eleven builds, and under these categories a one-line change to a PowerShell script would pay the same bill twice.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":null,"mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Re-categorised, and the row uncovered a harder blocker on the way. zagent update --category was READ by write.mjs but missing from the update flag allowlist in cli/legacy-pure/flags.mjs, so a mis-filed category could not be corrected through the CLI at all -- the only fix would have been delete-and-recreate. That is the same shape as the sprint --force comment sitting directly above it in that file, and the comment now names both instances. With the flag reachable, seven Tools-only ZEN tickets moved from Engine to Tooling: ZEN-74, 75, 76, 78, 83, 97, 98. MEASURED: each dropped from 15 gate lines to 12, and the 12 actually execute such a diff (the assert scripts and the Vault suite) rather than eleven C++ game builds plus a Combat test run. The wider board audit found no other ticket of this shape."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:09.125Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:09.125Z"},{"id":"cde8621f-8208-4b78-8ff0-0ef5f743977a","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"config","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Invariant I3 requires every tick to \"grep the decision log for the ticket's nouns before writing the prompt, and paste what you find VERBATIM\", and states that zagent.project.json \"already declares `decisionLog` and `decisionIdPrefix`, so you are told where the rulings live\".\n\nFor the Engine category it declares NEITHER. Only Zenithmon does. So on every Engine ticket the rulings clause of I3 is inert — there is nothing to grep.\n\nIt is not that Engine has no rulings. ZEN-19 was governed by a constraint recorded verbatim in Zenith/Flux/Shadows/CLAUDE.md — \"That hoist is load-bearing — the unified mesh cull's Prepare runs earlier in topological order (the cascades read its cull output), so a cascade-owned Prepare would hand it last frame's frusta\" — plus four code comments asserting the same placement by name. Nothing pointed the orchestrator at any of them; they were found by hand.\n\nSince the Vault now mints ZEN-D-* ids into the decisions database (ZEN-D-014 and ZEN-D-015 were filed during these two ticks), the missing piece is the DECLARATION, not the store.\n\nAlready tracked as ZEN-82 and ZEN-96 — filed here because ZEN-19 is a concrete measurement of what its absence costs.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"On ZEN-19 the governing rationale had to be assembled by hand into .zagent/run/ZEN-19/rulings.md before a worker could be dispatched under I3. A worker dispatched without it would have had no way to know the frame ORDER was load-bearing — and moving the call is precisely the obvious-looking refactor the ticket asks for.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-19","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed. The Engine category now declares decisionLog Zenith/Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md and decisionIdPrefix ZEN-D-, and that file was created, modelled on the Zenithmon log structure. The prefix was verified against what is already minted rather than guessed: ZEN-D-003/004/006/010-015 already appear in Zenith/Docs/Board/tickets. Those predate the file and are NOT backfilled; entries from here on land in both places. No project-level fallback was added, deliberately: every other category either files on a different board project (DP/UV/HE/FD) or has none of its own, so a single ZEN-D- default would misattribute their rulings under the wrong prefix. DevilsPlayground has a DecisionLog.md but its entries carry no ID convention at all, so declaring a prefix for it would invent one rather than record it. Also see the paired row on the same subject, resolved alongside this one."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:14.842Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:14.842Z"},{"id":"17830c07-c26f-4c72-82e8-01f395f1fd2b","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"tick","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"`Tools/zagent/build_prompt.ps1` quotes the ROOT C++ conventions into every worker prompt regardless of category. On ZEN-99 — a Node/Vitest ticket touching only Tools/Vault/**.mjs — the prompt's Conventions block opened with:\n\n  \"Root CLAUDE.md is binding. No std:: containers; every .cpp starts with #include \\\"Zenith.h\\\"; tabs; braces on new lines; Zenith_Assert is the real assert... Never run Sharpmake in a worktree.\"\n\nand only then gave the Tooling conventions, which are correct and say the opposite where they overlap (\"Tools/Vault is Node: ESM .mjs, Vitest... and NOT the engine's C++ naming rules\").\n\nUnder I3 everything pasted becomes the worker's instructions verbatim, and tick.md is explicit that a stale or inapplicable line \"does not sit there harmlessly: it competes with everything else in the prompt\". A worker cannot tell which half is current because it has no shell and no board.\n\nSuggest the root conventions be emitted only for categories whose paths are C++, or that the category's own conventions REPLACE rather than follow them.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Worked around by hand: a parenthetical was appended to the dispatched prompt saying the C++ conventions are quoted for every ticket and are irrelevant to this one. That worked, but it is a correction the orchestrator has to remember to make, on every non-engine ticket, with nothing to catch it if forgotten.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"nuisance","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-99","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed, and the fix is finer-grained than the row proposed. Emitting the category conventions INSTEAD of the root list would have dropped two clauses that are not C++ rules at all: \"Root CLAUDE.md is binding\" and \"Never run Sharpmake in a worktree\" -- the latter now MORE reachable from Tooling, not less, since Build/** joined the Engine category paths in the same change. So the project conventions split in two: a universal string that is always emitted, and a languageConventions string carrying the C++ clauses, which a category may suppress by declaring suppressLanguageConventions true. Tooling now declares it. resolveRules in cli/legacy-pure/routing.mjs composes universal + (language unless suppressed) + category. MEASURED against the real selector: a Tooling prompt now opens with the two universal clauses then its own Node/Vitest text, with no \"No std:: containers\" clause anywhere; Engine and Zenithmon are unchanged."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:20.447Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:20.447Z"},{"id":"148edb70-3a4b-4762-adcf-37c5003b9c14","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"other","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"`Tools/phototour_run.ps1` depends on Python Pillow through `Tools/phototour_crop.py`, and nothing in the repo declares that dependency — no requirements.txt, no check in the script, no mention in the harness header.\n\nOn a machine without it the failure shape is the expensive one: the tour ran to completion, captured all 11 shots, printed `DONE: 11 shots in ...`, and THEN exited 1 from the crop step with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL'`. The captures survive, but no .png crops and no compare sheet are produced, so the exit code is a real failure after several minutes of GPU work.\n\nThe script already guards the interpreter itself — it checks for `python` on PATH after the tour \"so a missing interpreter never costs a capture run\" and prints the manual re-crop command. The module check is the same class of problem and is not guarded. Suggest either a preflight `python -c \"import PIL\"` alongside the existing `Get-Command python` check (before the tour, so it costs no capture run), or a declared requirements file.\n\nRecovery is cheap once known: `python -m pip install pillow`, then re-run `python Tools\\phototour_crop.py <outDir>` — the script already prints that line.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Cost one full RenderTest photo-tour run on ZEN-19 before the failure surfaced, and the failure appeared AFTER the success banner, which made it read initially as a teardown fault rather than a missing dependency.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"done","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-19","mjyvbwb8eb566wiwz1qx9z57":"Fixed as suggested, with the preflight option rather than a requirements file. Tools/phototour_run.ps1:79-97 now checks Get-Command python AND python -c \"import PIL\" BEFORE the capture run, failing with the recovery line (python -m pip install pillow). The existing post-tour interpreter check stays as the late safety net for an interpreter that vanishes mid-run, with its comment reworded to say so. Dependency declared in the harness header (:11-15) rather than Tools/requirements-ci.txt: that file is consumed only by layering-gate.yml and complexity.yml for tree-sitter static analysis, and phototour_run.ps1 appears in no workflow (it needs a windowed Vulkan_*_True GPU build), so adding Pillow there would imply CI runs this script and would install an unused dependency on every CI job."},"created_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:26.148Z","updated_at":"2026-09-20T22:31:26.148Z"},{"id":"7f594ca7-50f0-4944-b6e0-e334a0cf9781","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"cli","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Give build_prompt.ps1's -Rulings the same comma-splitting normalisation -Files already has. Lines 222-244 explain in detail that 'pwsh -File child.ps1 -Files a,b' collapses the comma-array into ONE string, and normalise $Files accordingly at line 236 — but $Rulings, declared [string[]] three lines below $Files, gets no such pass. So the documented invocation form works for one array parameter and silently fails for the other.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"tick.md step 5 mandates 'pwsh -NoProfile -File Tools/zagent/build_prompt.ps1 ... [-Rulings <path1>,<path2>,...]' — the exact form that cannot work. On ZEN-20 the call failed with '-Rulings path a.md,b.md does not exist', and the workaround was to concatenate the two rulings files into one before re-running. Cost 3 failed invocations. The failure is at least LOUD (the path does not exist), unlike the -Files case the existing normalisation was written to fix, but the asymmetry means the script half-honours its own documented CLI.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"new","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-20"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T00:46:58.110Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T00:46:58.110Z"},{"id":"fa5c7e0b-af1b-466e-a010-44cc04d87c36","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-016","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"The Engine gate list runs only 'test Combat --headless', and Combat has NO test that drives an editor deferred scene load — so no Engine gate executes Zenith_Editor::ProcessDeferredSceneOperations at all. The repo's one purpose-built cover for that path is Games/DevilsPlayground/Tests/Test_EditorSceneCycle.cpp (four teardowns: two registered-scene loads, two Play->Stop backup restores, with frames in flight), and it carries m_bRequiresGraphics = false, so it RUNS HEADLESS and costs one 'zenith build DevilsPlayground --headless' plus a ~10s boot. Any ticket touching the editor scene-load or frame-submit path should run it BY HAND and record the result; green Engine gates say nothing about that path.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Measured on ZEN-20, which removed the render-submit skip that fired on exactly those frames. All 15 Engine gate lines went green — 11 builds, test Combat, 2706/2706 units, two doc_lints — having executed ZERO frames on which the changed branch is reachable. The reviewer found the DP test; the hand run then returned '[AutomatedTest] Test_EditorSceneCycle: PASSED (601 frames, 9467.9 ms)', which is the only real evidence the change is safe. This is the same family as ZEN-D-003 (a RenderTest automated test is compile-checked by every gate list and run by none), but worse in one respect: here the uncovered path is in ENGINE code that every game links, and the covering test already exists and is cheap. Two mechanical notes for whoever runs it: the verdict line goes to STDOUT, not to Logs/zenith_*.log, so grepping the log finds nothing; and per ZEN-D-004 the boot re-authors Games/DevilsPlayground/Assets/Scenes/ProcLevel.zscen every time, which must be git-restored before staging.","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"none — this records a gap, not a fixed behaviour","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-20","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T01:23:50.792Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T01:23:50.792Z"},{"id":"e238a465-7026-4970-8aac-ded14a990008","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-017","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"The three deferred scene-load branches of Zenith_Editor::ProcessDeferredSceneOperations do NOT share a loading mechanism, and 'Zenith_SceneSystem::LoadScene is synchronous' does not cover all three. The registered-scene-index branch and the load-from-file branch go through LoadSceneByIndex / LoadScene, which ARE synchronous including Awake/OnEnable lifecycle dispatch. HandlePendingSceneLoad — the Play->Stop backup restore and Open Scene, i.e. the MOST FREQUENT of the three — does not: it reaches Zenith_EditorSceneAccess::LoadFromFile -> Zenith_SceneData::LoadFromFile directly, and its only LoadScene call is SCENE_LOAD_ADDITIVE_WITHOUT_LOADING, which does no file I/O. That path dispatches NO lifecycle at all, by design and by its own comment in Zenith_SceneData_Serialization.cpp ('Lifecycle dispatch is handled by LoadScene after this method returns. Do NOT dispatch here to avoid double-dispatch'). It IS still wholly synchronous — Reset -> ReadFromFile -> LoadFromDataStream -> TransitionTo(SCENE_STATE_LOADED) — which is usually the property an argument actually needs.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Measured on ZEN-20. The worker's safety argument for always-submitting render work asserted that every false-returning branch runs 'file read, deserialise, Awake/OnEnable, flip to LOADED' and cited ZenithECS/CLAUDE.md's 'LoadScene is synchronous'. The conclusion was right and the citation was wrong for the branch that fires most often. Nothing mechanical catches this: both statements are true of two branches out of three, the wrong one is the common case, and a future auditor going to ZenithECS/CLAUDE.md finds the sentence and stops. Anyone reasoning about what is complete after a deferred editor scene load must distinguish SYNCHRONY (all three) from LIFECYCLE DISPATCH (two of three).","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"Test_EditorSceneCycle (DevilsPlayground) exercises both shapes — two registered-scene loads and two Play->Stop backup restores — but asserts nothing about lifecycle dispatch specifically.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-20","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T01:24:33.932Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T01:24:33.932Z"},{"id":"be30f9e3-4721-4af6-9dc2-ad8c0a29de5f","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-018","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"Flux_Primitives has producers on BOTH sides of Zenith_Core.cpp's SubmitRenderWork seam, so ZEN-D-005's hazard reaches further than the debug-variable toggle it was written about. Zenith_AI::DebugDraw() submits on the debug channel from inside UpdateGameLogic — BEFORE SubmitRenderWork — and gameplay components submit on the gameplay channel from the same place, while BOTH channels are retired only by Flux_PrimitivesImpl::ConsumeFrameBoundary inside the GBuffer pass, i.e. only if ExecuteRenderGraph runs. The producers that sit INSIDE SubmitRenderWork (Zenith_PhysicsDebugDraw::QueueAll, Zenith_SceneGraphDebug::QueueOverlays, RebuildSceneSnapshot, UI().Update()) are skipped alongside the drain and cannot accumulate. So: never gate ExecuteRenderGraph on a per-frame skip condition. Anything that would skip the graph must either also suppress every producer that runs earlier in the frame, or retire their queues explicitly.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Found on ZEN-20 by the reviewer, against an orchestrator comment that asserted the opposite ('the old early return was not an instance of that ruling'). Verified in the sources: Zenith_AI::DebugDraw() at Zenith_Core.cpp:232 inside UpdateGameLogic; ConsumeFrameBoundary called only from the GBuffer pass callback at Flux_Primitives.cpp:1040. The two co-occur in practice — the game-logic gate is recomputed from editor mode AFTER Editor().Update(), and a scene load does not change the mode, so a content-browser Open Scene while Playing queued primitives and then skipped their drain. It was BOUNDED at one frame, not unbounded like ZEN-40's photo tour, which is why it never overflowed the Vulkan scratch allocator and why nothing ever caught it. ZEN-20 removed the skip, so there is no live instance today; this records the structural fact so that re-introducing ANY render-skip is understood to re-introduce the hazard.","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"none — no test asserts the producer/drain split. ZEN-40 added the unconditional ConsumeFrameBoundary drain, which bounds the damage but does not prevent a new skip.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-20","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T01:24:59.766Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T01:24:59.766Z"},{"id":"26b6d671-b3f4-4a71-bc69-3a951c601379","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"config","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Either point ZEN's Engine category at a decisionLog that zagent decide actually writes to, or make Zenith/Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md say plainly that it is NOT the store and that 'zagent rows decisions' is. Right now the claim payload for a ZEN ticket carries decisionLog: 'Zenith/Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md' and decisionIdPrefix: 'ZEN-D-', while zagent decide warns 'ZEN's Engine category declares no decisionLog ... this row exists only on the board; a worker resolving rulings from disk (client.mjs rulings.md) will never see it.' Both cannot be right.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"tick.md I3 instructs every tick to grep the decision log for the ticket's nouns before writing the worker prompt, and names decisionLog as where the rulings live. On ZEN-20 that file is 54 lines containing one placeholder heading ('## YYYY-MM-DD -- ZEN-D-NNN -- <one-line summary>') and ZERO real entries, while 18 ZEN-D-* rows exist on the board. A tick that follows I3 literally greps the file, finds nothing, and dispatches with no rulings inlined. I only found ZEN-D-005 and ZEN-D-014 — both of which turned out to govern this ticket, one of them centrally — by dumping 'zagent rows decisions --json' and filtering it myself, which I3 does not tell anyone to do. The stated consequence in decide's own warning is the sharper one: a loop WORKER resolving rulings from disk will never see any of these rows at all.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"new","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-20"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T01:25:23.852Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T01:25:23.852Z"},{"id":"b5404990-686d-4c9d-a65e-5a63248eb597","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-019","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"Flux's generated shader headers use TWO handle naming conventions, and a survey that knows only one concludes the binding is missing. 'hg_x<Name>' is used for the SHARED spine bindings (set 0 Global, set 1 View/CSM/ShadowMatrices/LightBuffer/cluster/IBL) and for a few per-program textures whose Slang parameter already began 'g_x' (hg_xHeightMap, hg_xAnimationTex, hg_xPrevDisplacementTex). Plain 'h<Name>', CASE PRESERVED from the Slang parameter, is used for every binding the program owns -- hObjects, hDrawItems, hBladePool, hSkinConstants, hbindPose, hskinJobs. So the rule for deriving a handle from a binding name is: strip any leading 'g_x', then look for BOTH h<Stem> and hg_x<Stem>, and do not assume capitalisation.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Measured on ZEN-22, which migrated 71 by-name Bind* call sites onto typed handles. Grepping only for 'hg_x' resolved 17 of 47 distinct (feature, name) pairs and made the ticket look like it required a FluxCompiler codegen change to emit the missing 30 -- i.e. unbuildable as filed and a candidate for a scope block. Checking both conventions resolved 47 of 47. The failure mode is asymmetric and expensive: the wrong conclusion is 'this needs a bigger ticket', which costs a Block and a re-file, and nothing in the pipeline contradicts it because the generated headers genuinely are AUTO-GENERATED / DO NOT EDIT and a codegen gap would be a real reason to stop.","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"none -- this is a reading convention, not a behaviour. The generated headers are regenerated by FluxCompiler, so the convention could drift without any test noticing.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-22","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T02:23:51.740Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T02:23:51.740Z"},{"id":"2bb137c7-b6ac-4c44-913a-07546d60455b","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-020","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"The SAME Flux binding-handle identifier carries DIFFERENT set/binding values in different program namespaces of the same generated header, so choosing the wrong program's namespace compiles cleanly, passes the resource-kind assertion, passes every gate, and mis-binds the descriptor on a real GPU only. Measured in Vegetation.h: the velocity G-buffer program inserts hGrassPrevWindConstants at binding 1 and shifts the rest up one -- hBladePool is {3,1} in Grass_ToGBuffer but {3,2} in Grass_ToGBufferVelocity, hVisibleIndices {3,2} vs {3,3}, hTypeParams {3,3} vs {3,4}. In UnifiedMesh.h, hObjects is {3,0,STRUCTURED_BUFFER} in ToGBuffer/ToGBufferVelocity/ToShadowmap but {3,1,RW_STRUCTURED_BUFFER} in UnifiedMesh_Culling. CONSEQUENCE: any code that selects its shader at RECORD TIME must select its handles the same way. Flux_GrassImpl::RecordGBuffer picks base-vs-velocity from a runtime latch and therefore binds in two explicit arms, not one shared list.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Found while scoping ZEN-22 (71 by-name binds migrated to typed handles). No gate in this repo can catch a wrong-namespace handle: every gate line runs the Null_ backend, which issues no real descriptor writes, and the identifier exists in both namespaces so the compiler is satisfied. The check that does work is mechanical and cheap -- parse the generated header into namespace -> declared identifiers, then confirm every Namespace::hIdent usage in the migrated .cpp resolves in THAT namespace (aliases are function-local and reused: Flux_UnifiedMesh.cpp declares 'US' twice, as UnifiedMesh_Skinning and as UnifiedMesh_ToShadowmap, so the resolution must be scope-aware). 75 references were verified that way on ZEN-22, plus a Vulkan run with VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation enabled -- GrassShowcase, TAATemporalStability and HumanShowcase all passed with zero VUIDs, which is the only check that exercises the descriptor writes at all.","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"None automated. RenderTest GrassShowcase / TAATemporalStability / HumanShowcase on a Vulkan_*_True build with validation layers is the empirical check; no gate line runs any of them.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"hard","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-22","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T02:24:17.951Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T02:24:17.951Z"},{"id":"d7d9ffae-b43c-43e3-889b-b3ad6d51a868","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-021","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"NO gate in any category runs FluxCompiler, so nothing local checks (a) the two shader lints' walks over the real tree, or (b) the invariant that the generated shader tree is clean after a canonical run. Only .github/workflows/shader-validation.yml does, and CI does not run from a tick because push is false. CONSEQUENCE: a shader lint can be committed green and vacuous, and the committed .spv tree can drift stale, with every gate line passing. Any ticket that touches Zenith/Flux/Shaders/** or the Slang lints should build FluxCompiler by hand -- msbuild Build/zenith_engine_win64.sln /t:FluxCompiler /p:Configuration=Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True -- and RUN it, then check git status for regenerated .spv.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"Measured on ZEN-41, which added Flux_NormalDecodeLint. All 18 gate lines went green having never executed the lint's walk: the gates build FluxCompiler's dependencies but never invoke the exe. Running it by hand scanned 100 .slang files with 0 violations, and an anti-vacuity probe (an open-coded decode appended to a real shader) made it exit 1 with the correct file and line -- without that second step the 0 is indistinguishable from a lint that matches nothing. The same run also regenerated FOUR tracked .spv files. Hash-comparing consecutive runs showed all four byte-STABLE, so FluxCompiler output is deterministic and the committed versions were simply STALE; one of them, Flux_UnifiedMesh_Reset.csMain.spv, includes only Common/Bindings.slang and so could not have been affected by that ticket's MaterialSurface.slang edit -- its staleness predated the ticket and no gate would ever have reported it.","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"None. The 12 NormalDecodeLint units exercise the scanner in-process; nothing exercises the FluxCompiler walk or the generated-tree-clean invariant outside CI.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-41","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T03:26:30.235Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T03:26:30.235Z"},{"id":"be491f93-add0-4145-bd75-07c37e8cdeb9","database_id":"roqon5olpfp13m5xe4d9miq1","values":{"fm04r617ckxd7s4wv762wi0h":"ZEN-D-022","iv4c61wxv3wvh0jr0fjdcd6o":"2026-09-21","ofmpdviro4nuojcx5s7tinbk":"A ticket filed against a Suggestions row must be re-checked against that row's STATUS and RESOLUTION before it is claimed, because a resolved row's fix may already have shipped and the ticket will not know. ZEN-73 asked for a doc_lint check reconciling AssetManifest.md roster counts AND generator version stamps, citing a 2026-08-25 row. That row was already Status=done, and its Resolution describes C10 delivering exactly the version-stamp half plus prop roster arithmetic, with generators DISCOVERED by globbing Source/Gen/ZM_*Gen.h. So roughly half the ticket's stated deliverable existed, and its framing -- 'every generator bump has to be mirrored by hand and nothing reds when it is not' -- was false when the ticket was claimed. The ticket also asserted the new check would be C9; C9 and C10 were both taken.","kdiiph10osx2gugvy2m7phbp":"The remaining work was real -- C10 covered the PROP roster only, so species/human/building were unchecked, and six claims had drifted (props 25 vs 32, humans 34 vs 35) -- so this was not a duplicate to Block, but it was roughly half the size the ticket described and used a check id that would have collided. Reading the row cost one 'zagent suggestions --all' call and reframed the dispatch. DO NOT re-resolve an already-resolved row to satisfy a DoD box: this row's Resolution is a detailed, accurate record of C10's work, and overwriting it with one describing C11 would destroy a better record than the replacement. Say in the work log that the row was already closed and by what, and leave it.","xi9qknki9rqlrdtwlsj96lje":"None. No check compares a ticket body against the Suggestions row it cites, and the row carries no back-link to tickets filed from it.","svsmruplkrgighauooekv42e":"easy","lpd7518yykwmax9abxeyxag2":"ZEN-73","s42eqon7i4g5v28qulm03ctg":"engine"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T04:31:10.273Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T04:31:10.273Z"},{"id":"789f17b6-8c56-467d-94c1-0e82b2cae230","database_id":"cnjr4j9501dwnmtozwf03oo8","values":{"ohv88qhy9empasgx47noi40o":"gates","u3pk0xm44evvopgkhgn7txwg":"Add the two doc_lint assert scripts to the Tooling category's gate list in zagent.project.json: Tools/Test_DocLintRosterStamps.ps1 (C10, exists since that check landed) and Tools/Test_DocLintRosterCounts.ps1 (C11, added by ZEN-73). The Tooling list names its assert scripts individually and already includes Test_DocLintKeyCitations.ps1, so the pattern is established -- these two were simply never added. A human has to do it: zagent.project.json is a protectedPath.","o3pcxl3702jyekp99cz9u9tp":"Both scripts are real black-box harnesses over doc_lint.ps1 -- 17 and 9 assertions respectively, each with its own exit code -- and NOTHING runs either. On ZEN-73 the 28-line gate run included five doc_lint invocations and neither assert script, so a regression in C10's or C11's scraper would ship green: doc_lint itself would still pass on the CURRENT docs while its ability to CATCH drift went unverified. That is the vacuous-lint failure mode, and the assert scripts are precisely the control for it. I ran Test_DocLintRosterCounts.ps1 by hand (9/9) plus an anti-vacuity probe on the real docs, but a tick should not have to remember that.","q48d3r9i9zteonj2f3woqmft":"slows-work","z7u2ncb8npdpnzn30sl35zh8":"new","v0my4v0v58jap2rq2zldbis1":"ZEN-73"},"created_at":"2026-09-21T04:31:32.252Z","updated_at":"2026-09-21T04:31:32.252Z"}],"notion.databases":[{"id":"bbzp9x5hxhxy33hktm4s5obc","title":"Agent
